apps.scheduledCommandsHelp: A nightly report, an hourly cleanup. Each runs on its own, in this app's image, on the schedule you give it.

apps.noVolumesHelp: An app writes to a disk when its files have to outlive a deployment — uploads, a database it runs itself, a cache worth keeping.
apps.deleteVolumeConfirm: This deletes the disk mounted at {{path}} and everything on it.
apps.deleteVolumeConsequence: The files cannot be recovered afterwards. Take a backup first if you might need them.
apps.deleteVolumeLastBackup: The last working backup of this disk was {{when}}. Anything written since then goes with it.
apps.deleteVolumeNeverBackedUp: This disk has never been backed up. Everything on it is gone for good.

apps.volumeBackupsHelp: A schedule, the copies taken so far, and putting one back.
apps.noVolumeBackups: No backups of this disk yet.
apps.volumeRestoreStarted: The restore has started. The app stops while it runs and starts again afterwards.
apps.volumeRestoreWarning: Everything on {{app}} is replaced by what was in this backup, and the app is stopped while that happens.
apps.volumeStopsRollingDeploys: A disk means deploys are no longer seamless
apps.volumeStopsRollingDeploysHelp: One disk can only be written by one instance at a time, so Skifity stops the old instance before starting the new one. Each deploy has a few seconds with nothing answering, and the app cannot run more than one instance.
apps.lockDeploysHelp: Stops every deploy and rollback of this app — from here, the CLI, an assistant or a push — until somebody unlocks it. Changing variables or instances still applies.
apps.usageHelp: The busiest instance as a share of its own limit, read every minute and kept for three days. The dashed line is where a warning is sent.

apps.alertsHelp: Sent to the team's notification channels once when a threshold is crossed for three minutes, and once when it is over. 0 turns one off.

apps.healthCheckTcp: TCP: check the port is open

A deploy is then zero-downtime only if the app is ready the moment it starts. Use this only for software that cannot answer a check.
apps.healthStartHelp: How long a new instance may take before it has to answer, from {{min}} to {{max}}. Two minutes suits most apps; a JVM, or an image that migrates its database before it listens, may need five to ten.
apps.healthTimeoutHelp: How long one check waits for an answer, from {{min}} to {{max}}.

apps.trafficHelp: What reached the app through its domains, counted by the ingress every minute and kept for three days. A request the firewall, maintenance or a password answered never reached the app and is not counted.
apps.trafficPartial: Some minutes are missing part of their requests: the ingress on one of the servers did not answer.

trafficWhy.notRouted: This app has no domain, so nothing reaches it through the ingress. Requests from the environment's other apps are not counted.
trafficWhy.starting: The panel started counting requests a moment ago. The first minute appears after the second reading, about two minutes from now.
trafficWhy.reading: No requests have been counted for this app in this period yet.
trafficWhy.no_traefik: There is no Traefik in the cluster's kube-system namespace, so requests cannot be counted. Skifity counts them from the Traefik that k3s installs.
trafficWhy.unreachable: Traefik did not answer on its metrics port, 9100, so requests are not being counted. If you configure Traefik yourself, keep its Prometheus metrics on.
trafficWhy.no_cluster: The panel is not connected to a cluster, so there is nothing to count requests from.

apps.alertsErrorsHelp: Server errors are only judged over three minutes with at least 20 requests between them, so one failed request on a quiet app is not a warning.

domains.certificateFailed: The certificate could not be issued

domains.cannotRemoveAutomatic: The automatic domain cannot be removed. It keeps the app reachable while you set up your own.
domains.dnsUnknown: Nobody has told this panel which public address its apps answer on. An administrator can set it under Settings, Domains.
domains.removeDomainConfirm: {{hostname}} stops reaching this app. Visitors get an error until you add it back or point it somewhere else.
domains.dnsIntro: Add this record at whoever manages your domain's DNS — your registrar, or Cloudflare if you use it.
domains.dnsPropagation: A new record usually works within a few minutes, and can take a few hours.
domains.dnsNameVaries: Some registrars want the whole name here; others want only the part in front of your domain.
domains.dnsStatusPartly: DNS points here only in part
domains.dnsHereHelp: Visitors who use this address reach this app.
domains.dnsPartlyHelp: {{addresses}} is not this cluster, so some visitors reach this app and some do not. Remove that record, or change it to {{expected}}.
domains.dnsElsewhereHelp: Change the record to {{expected}}. The old address keeps getting visitors until you do.
domains.dnsMissingHelp: Nothing answers for this name yet. Create the record, and check again in a few minutes.
domains.dnsUnknownHelp: This panel does not know its own public address, so it cannot tell whether that is here. An administrator can set it under Settings, Domains.
domains.dnsCertificateSoon: The certificate is issued once DNS points here, so it should follow within a few minutes.
domains.dnsCertificateAfter: The certificate is issued once DNS points here.
domains.redirectHelp: Visitors to {{hostname}} are sent to {{target}} permanently, with the same path. Search engines move the page to {{target}} too.
domains.ownCertificateRenew: Nothing renews a certificate you brought. Renew it with the authority that issued it and upload it under the same name: every app using it is updated.

scaling.title: Scaling
scaling.automaticHelp: Skifity adds and removes instances between the numbers below, by how busy the app is.
scaling.scaleToZero: Stop when nobody is using it
scaling.scaleToZeroHelp: The app stops after a few idle minutes and starts again on the first request. The first request after that takes a few seconds.
scaling.scaleToZeroUsesRequests: While this is on, the app is scaled by how many requests are waiting rather than by CPU or memory. The most instances still applies.
scaling.readinessOk: This app looks ready to run several instances.
scaling.resourcesHelp: Reserved is what each instance is guaranteed. The limit is the most it may use before it is restarted.
scaling.spreadHelp: Instances are placed on different servers where possible, so losing one server does not take the app down.

file_cache.title: The cache is stored on local disk
file_cache.detail: {{0}} is set to {{1}}, so each instance would have its own cache and they would disagree.
file_cache.fix: Use Redis for the cache, or accept that cached values differ between instances.

in_memory_sessions.title: Sessions are kept in memory or on disk
in_memory_sessions.detail: {{0}} is set to {{1}}. Each instance would keep its own sessions, so users would be signed out at random as requests land on different instances.
in_memory_sessions.fix: Create a Redis database in this environment and point the session store at it. Skifity links it in as a variable for you.

in_process_cron.title: Scheduled jobs run inside the app
in_process_cron.detail: {{0}} is on. With several instances, every instance runs the schedule, so each job runs several times.
in_process_cron.fix: Run the scheduler as a separate app with one instance, or use a lock so only one instance runs each job.

local_uploads.title: Uploaded files are written to local disk
local_uploads.detail: {{0}} points at a directory inside the container. Files written by one instance would be invisible to the others, and would disappear on the next deploy.
local_uploads.fix: Store uploads in S3-compatible object storage. MinIO is available as a one-click template if you would rather not use a cloud provider.

memory_target_below_idle.title: The memory target is reached before the app does anything
memory_target_below_idle.detail: The target is a percentage of what this app reserves. It reserves {{0}}Mi and the target is {{1}}%, so a new instance is added above {{2}}Mi — which a Node or JVM process passes at startup.
memory_target_below_idle.fix: Raise the reserved memory under the app's settings to what the app uses when it is idle, plus room to work. Memory does not fall once it has been claimed, so a target below the idle figure never comes back down.

no_health_check.title: There is no health check path
no_health_check.detail: Without one, Skifity can only check that the port is open, which happens before most frameworks are ready to serve.
no_health_check.fix: Add a path such as /healthz that returns 200 once the app is ready, and set it under the app's settings.

no_metrics.title: The cluster is not reporting CPU and memory
no_metrics.detail: Autoscaling on a CPU or memory target reads those numbers from metrics-server, and nothing is answering. The app will stay at its minimum number of instances however busy it gets, and nothing will say so.
no_metrics.fix: k3s installs metrics-server by default. Check that it is running in kube-system, or set a fixed number of instances until it is.

single_instance.title: This app runs as a single instance
single_instance.detail: If the server it is on restarts, the app is unavailable until Kubernetes starts it somewhere else.
single_instance.fix: Raise the number of instances to two, or turn on autoscaling, once the points above are addressed.

sqlite.title: This app uses SQLite
sqlite.detail: {{0}} points at a SQLite file. SQLite is a single file on one disk, so instances on different servers cannot share it.
sqlite.fix: Create a PostgreSQL database in this environment and point the app at it. Skifity injects the connection string for you.

target_below_idle.title: The CPU target is reached before the app does anything
target_below_idle.detail: The target is a percentage of what this app reserves, not of the server. It reserves {{0}}m of CPU and the target is {{1}}%, so a new instance is added above {{2}}m — about a tenth of one core, which most frameworks pass while idle.
target_below_idle.fix: Raise the reserved CPU under the app's settings to what it actually uses when busy, so the percentage means something. The reservation is what the app is guaranteed, not a limit on it.

volume.title: This app writes to a disk that only one instance can use
volume.detail: A volume is mounted at {{0}}. That storage can be attached to one server at a time, so a second instance would either fail to start or end up on the same server.
volume.fix: Move uploads to object storage such as S3 or MinIO, or turn on cross-node storage in Settings so the volume can be shared. Until then, keep this app at one instance.

volume_with_replicas.title: More than one instance is configured, and this app has a volume
volume_with_replicas.detail: The extra instances will stay pending, or will be scheduled onto the same server and write to the same files at once.
volume_with_replicas.fix: Set the instance count back to one, or enable cross-node storage, or move the data out of the volume.

health_check_off.title: The health check is off
health_check_off.detail: Each instance is sent traffic as soon as its process starts, whether it is ready or not, and one that stops answering keeps receiving requests. With several instances, some visitors get errors and others do not.
health_check_off.fix: Turn the health check on under the app's settings: HTTP with a path that returns 200 once the app is ready, or TCP if it has no such path.

servers.title: Servers
servers.subtitle: The machines your apps run on. Skifity joins them into one cluster.
servers.addServerIntro: Enter the address and how to sign in. {{product}} does the rest.
servers.authKeyPlaceholder: Paste the contents of your private key file
servers.passwordNotStored: Your password is used once, to install a key {{product}} owns, and is never stored.
servers.serverNameHelp: Something you will recognise, such as "Frankfurt 1".
servers.locationHelp: A label, so you can place apps near your users.
servers.controlPlaneHelp: Control plane servers run the cluster itself. Three of them keep it working when one fails.
servers.emptyHelp: Any VPS with Ubuntu or Debian works. One server is enough to start.
servers.requirementsList: Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 12, at least 1 GB of memory, 8 GB of free disk, and SSH access as root.
servers.promote: Make it a control plane server
servers.promoteHelp: With three control plane servers, the cluster survives losing one. This moves the apps off this server first.
servers.removeServerWarning: Instances running here move to your other servers first. Nothing is lost.
servers.wipeServer: Also remove Kubernetes from the machine
servers.adopted: Skifity did not install this server
servers.adoptedHelp: It was already a node of the cluster when Skifity was installed — usually the machine the panel itself runs on. It is shown here so you can see what the cluster has, and it cannot be removed or promoted from the panel, because there is no key to it. Run the uninstaller on the machine itself to take it out.

servers.usageNone: Nothing recorded yet. The panel reads every ready server once a minute.

hardening.title: Hardening
hardening.description: How this server stands up to the internet. Checked over SSH when you ask, and nothing on the server is changed by checking.
hardening.passwordsOffTitle: Turn off SSH passwords on this server?
hardening.passwordsOffHelp: SSH on this server still accepts passwords. Skifity signs in with a key, so it can turn them off safely.
hardening.passwordsOffConfirm: Signing in to this server over SSH will need a key from then on, for everybody, and root will be able to sign in with a key only. Keep your own key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys before you do this. The change is checked before SSH reloads, and undone if it does not take.

unknown.detail: The SSH daemon's settings could not be read, so whether it takes passwords is not known.
unknown.fix: Run sshd -T | grep -i passwordauthentication on the server as root.

on.detail: SSH accepts passwords, so anybody on the internet can keep guessing one.
on.fix: Turn SSH passwords off; Skifity signs in with a key, so nothing it does needs them.

password.detail: root can sign in over SSH with a password.
password.fix: Allow root keys only (PermitRootLogin prohibit-password); turning SSH passwords off does that too.

none.detail: root cannot sign in over SSH.

key.detail: root can sign in over SSH with a key only.

active.detail: fail2ban is running and bans addresses that keep failing to sign in.

inactive.detail: fail2ban is installed and not running.

absent.fix: Install it (apt install fail2ban, or dnf install fail2ban), or turn SSH passwords off, which leaves nothing to guess.

off.detail: Automatic updates are installed and turned off.
off.fix: Turn them on: dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades, or enable dnf-automatic-install.timer.

absent.detail: Nothing installs security updates on this server by itself.
absent.fix: Install unattended-upgrades (Debian, Ubuntu) or dnf-automatic (Fedora, RHEL and their kin).

none.detail: No firewall is active, so every port a process opens is open to the internet.
none.fix: Retry the server's setup, which configures the firewall, or enable ufw with ports 22, 80 and 443 open.

required.detail: Updates are installed that take effect only after a reboot.
required.fix: Reboot the server at a quiet moment; with more than one server, one at a time.

databases.title: Databases
databases.subtitle: Managed databases, backed up and connected to your apps.
databases.storageHelp: How much disk the database gets. This can be increased later, but not reduced.
databases.emptyHelp: A managed database is backed up, restored and connected to your apps for you.
databases.credentialsWarning: Anyone with these can read and change everything in the database.
databases.linkAppHelp: The connection string is added to the app as a variable, and the app is restarted so it picks it up.
databases.backupScheduleFieldHelp: When the backup runs. Times are UTC.
databases.retentionHelp: Older backups are deleted when a new one succeeds.
databases.backupScheduleHelp: Backups are written to the storage you configured in Settings.
databases.restoreWarning: This replaces everything currently in the database with the contents of this backup. It cannot be undone.
databases.restoreStarted: Restore started. The database is unavailable until it finishes.
databases.deleteWarning: Every table, row and backup schedule goes with it. Existing backups in your storage are kept, but the panel will no longer know about them.
databases.backupStarted: The backup has started. It will appear in the list when it finishes.
databases.unlinkConfirm: {{app}} loses the {{variable}} variable, so it cannot reach this database from its next deployment onwards.
databases.fromYourComputerHint: The host above answers only inside the cluster. This command opens a port on your computer that reaches the database through the panel, for psql, a desktop client or a migration.

engineHelp.postgres: Relational and dependable: the one to pick when unsure. It can run as several instances for failover.
engineHelp.mysql: MySQL itself, from Oracle's image, for software that asks for MySQL by name.
engineHelp.mariadb: MySQL-compatible, and what most PHP software is tested with.
engineHelp.mongodb: Documents rather than tables, for apps written for MongoDB.
engineHelp.redis: In-memory keys and values, for caches, queues and sessions.
engineHelp.valkey: Redis's open-source continuation. Apps use it exactly as they use Redis.
engineHelp.dragonfly: Speaks the Redis protocol and uses every core. It saves a snapshot every five minutes.
engineHelp.clickhouse: Column-oriented, for analytics over large tables.
engineHelp.memcached: A cache and nothing more: no disk, no password, and only this environment's apps reach it.

noBackupsReason.dragonfly: Dragonfly does not implement the command a live snapshot is taken through from outside the server, and its own snapshots stay on its own disk. It saves one every five minutes and as it stops, so a restart loses nothing, but a lost disk loses everything.
noBackupsReason.clickhouse: ClickHouse's own BACKUP command writes to a bucket with the bucket's keys inside the database, and Skifity never hands those to an environment. Back it up yourself with BACKUP ... TO S3, or keep its tables rebuildable from their source.
noBackupsReason.memcached: Memcached is a cache: it keeps everything in memory and nothing on a disk, so there is nothing to back up. Whatever is in it is gone when it restarts, by design.

databases.nativeConnectionStringHint: For clients that speak ClickHouse's own protocol, such as clickhouse-client and clickhouse-go. The connection string above is HTTP, which most client libraries take.
databases.noCredentials: Memcached has no user and no password. Only the apps in this environment can reach it.

templates.title: Templates
templates.subtitle: Applications that install in one step, with their databases and settings already connected.
templates.installedNote: Installed. It may take a minute to start.
templates.installedApps_one: Installed {{count}} app. It may take a minute to start.
templates.installedApps_other: Installed {{count}} apps. They may take a minute to start.

catalogues.title: Template catalogues
catalogues.help: Your team's own templates, from a file published at an https address. They appear beside the built-in ones for this team only, are held to the same checks, and are downloaded again every day.
catalogues.empty: This team has no catalogues of its own yet.
catalogues.name: Name
catalogues.nameHelp: The badge on each of its templates.
catalogues.urlHelp: The raw file, over https: a YAML or JSON index, or a .tar.gz or .zip of templates. Not a token: that goes in the header.
catalogues.headerHelp: For a private Git host only: Authorization, or PRIVATE-TOKEN for GitLab. The value is sealed, sent only to the catalogue's own host, and never shown again.
catalogues.removeConfirm: Its templates leave this page. Apps already installed from it keep running, and are no longer offered its updates.
catalogues.lastError: The last refresh failed. The copy downloaded before is still the one templates install from.
catalogues.notice_one: {{count}} template in your catalogues cannot be installed.
catalogues.notice_other: {{count}} templates in your catalogues cannot be installed.
catalogues.staleNotice_one: {{count}} catalogue could not be refreshed, and its last good copy is still in use.
catalogues.staleNotice_other: {{count}} catalogues could not be refreshed, and their last good copies are still in use.

settings.title: Settings
settings.roleHelp: Owners can do anything, including removing the team. Admins manage servers and settings. Members deploy apps. Viewers can see everything a member can and change nothing.
settings.secretStored: Stored. Enter a new value to replace it.
settings.componentsHelp: Heavy features are installed only when you first use them, so a fresh install stays small.
settings.rotateKeyHelp: Creates a new master key and re-encrypts every stored secret with it. Your secrets are not decrypted in the process.
settings.auditLogHelp: Who did what, when, and from where.
settings.noUpdateCheck: {{product}} does not contact any server to check for updates.
settings.rotateKeyDone: The master key was rotated and every stored secret was re-encrypted with it.
settings.rotateKeyPartial: The new master key is in place, but some secrets could not be re-encrypted. The old key was kept so they stay readable — keep your previous recovery key as well until a rotation finishes cleanly, because the new one does not open them.
settings.subtitle: Everything an operator configures, in one place. Nothing here needs a file on the server.
settings.inviteLinkHelp: It is shown once, works for seven days, and can only be used once. Skifity does not send email unless you have configured SMTP.
settings.inviteMemberHelp: Invite somebody by email. Skifity gives you a link to send them; they choose their own password. Somebody who already has an account here is added directly instead.
settings.exportHelp: Everything this team has — projects, apps, domains, databases, variables and schedules — as one JSON file, with each app's Kubernetes objects beside it.
settings.exportSecrets: The value of anything marked secret is not included. Those values are already in your own cluster, as ordinary Kubernetes Secrets you have access to.
settings.pluginStoreCheckHelp: Reads the catalogue with the values as they are saved, so a wrong address or a wrong key turns up here rather than on the day you wanted a plugin.
settings.pluginStoreVerified: Signed by the key set here
settings.pluginStoreGoToPlugins: Go to Plugins to install one

cluster_flannel_backend.label: How servers talk to each other
cluster_flannel_backend.help: WireGuard encrypts traffic between your servers, which matters when they are with different providers. It needs the wireguard kernel module on every server. vxlan works everywhere and is not encrypted. Every server in a cluster has to use the same one, so change this before adding servers, not after.

cluster_k3s_version.label: Kubernetes version
cluster_k3s_version.help: The k3s version the first server of a new cluster is installed with. Leave empty to follow the stable channel. A server added later joins at the version the cluster is running, whatever this says, because a server newer than its cluster is not supported.

cluster_preview_ttl_days.label: Remove preview environments after
cluster_preview_ttl_days.help: Days with no deployment before a pull request's preview environment is removed. A preview that is still being pushed to survives however long the pull request stays open. Set to 0 to keep them until their pull request closes, which is how previews are normally removed — but a webhook that never arrives then leaves one running forever.

dns_api_token.label: DNS API token
dns_api_token.help: A token scoped to edit records in one zone. Do not use a global account key.

dns_provider.label: DNS provider
dns_provider.help: Lets Skifity create DNS records for you when you add a domain. Leave empty to create them yourself.

dns_zone.label: DNS zone
dns_zone.help: The zone records are created in.

domains_acme_email.label: Let's Encrypt email
domains_acme_email.help: Where Let's Encrypt sends certificate expiry warnings. Required before HTTPS certificates can be issued.

domains_acme_server.label: ACME directory URL
domains_acme_server.help: Leave empty for Let's Encrypt production. Point it at the staging directory while you are testing, so you do not hit the rate limit.

domains_cloudflare_tunnel_token.label: Cloudflare tunnel token
domains_cloudflare_tunnel_token.help: Lets your apps answer on the internet without a public IP, a port open, or a fixed address for DNS to point at. Create a tunnel in the Cloudflare dashboard under Zero Trust, Networks, Tunnels; choose the Cloudflared connector and copy the token it shows. Then add one public hostname on that tunnel — a wildcard such as *.apps.example.com covers every app at once — with the service set to HTTP and the address traefik.kube-system.svc.cluster.local:80. Install Cloudflare tunnel under Components once the token is saved.

domains_cluster_ip.label: Cluster public IP
domains_cluster_ip.help: The address your domains should point at. Detected automatically; override it if your cluster sits behind a load balancer.

domains_geo_asn_url.label: Network database
domains_geo_asn_url.help: The same, for the network a visitor's address belongs to, which is what an AS number rule tests.

domains_geo_country_url.label: Country database
domains_geo_country_url.help: Where the firewall's country data comes from, in MaxMind's .mmdb format. Leave empty for DB-IP's free monthly file, which needs no account. A %s in the address is replaced with the month. Point it at your own copy, or at a MaxMind download, if you would rather.

domains_geo_enabled.label: Look up a visitor's country and network
domains_geo_enabled.help: On by default. The firewall downloads DB-IP's free monthly databases, which need no account, so that a rule can name a country or a network. Turn it off on a cluster with no way out to the internet, or if you would rather nothing was downloaded — a rule about a country cannot then be saved, which is better than one that is quietly skipped.

domains_trusted_proxies.label: Trusted proxies
domains_trusted_proxies.help: Address ranges in front of this cluster that may say who a visitor is. The pod and service networks are trusted already; add a load balancer's range here if you have one. Get this wrong in the other direction and a visitor can choose the address your firewall rules judge them by, so add only ranges you control.

domains_wildcard.label: Wildcard domain
domains_wildcard.help: A domain with a wildcard DNS record pointing at this cluster. Every app gets a free subdomain under it. Leave empty to use sslip.io addresses instead.

email_smtp_from.label: Send email from
email_smtp_from.help: The address notifications appear to come from. It usually has to be one your mail server is allowed to send as, or the mail is rejected.

email_smtp_host.label: SMTP host
email_smtp_host.help: Needed for email notifications and for password reset emails.

email_smtp_password.label: SMTP password
email_smtp_password.help: Stored encrypted. Most providers want an app password here rather than your account password.

email_smtp_port.label: SMTP port
email_smtp_port.help: 587 for STARTTLS, which is what almost everything uses now. 465 is implicit TLS; 25 is unencrypted and usually blocked by hosting providers.

email_smtp_tls.label: Use STARTTLS
email_smtp_tls.help: Leave on unless your mail server only accepts plain connections.

email_smtp_user.label: SMTP username
email_smtp_user.help: Leave empty if your mail server accepts mail from this cluster without signing in.

general_default_builder.label: Default builder
general_default_builder.help: Which builder to use when a repository has no Dockerfile. Railpack is the one available: Nixpacks was replaced by Railpack, and its command line is not published as an image a build can run.

general_panel_url.label: Panel URL
general_panel_url.help: The address people use to reach this panel. Used in links inside notifications and in webhook URLs.

general_telemetry_disabled.label: Disable usage reporting
general_telemetry_disabled.help: Skifity sends nothing anywhere by default. This setting exists so that the absence of telemetry is visible rather than assumed.

maintenance_audit_history_days.label: Keep the activity log for
maintenance_audit_history_days.help: Days. The activity log is kept far longer than anything else here, because a log that forgets is most of the way to not having one. Shorten it only if you have a reason to.

maintenance_deployment_history.label: Deployment records to keep, per app
maintenance_deployment_history.help: How many past deployments an app keeps, with their build logs. Older ones are removed so the panel's database does not grow without end. Only the ten most recent can be rolled back to, because that is how many images the registry keeps and how many revisions Kubernetes itself remembers.

plugins_store_public_key.label: Plugin store signing key
plugins_store_public_key.help: The store's Ed25519 public key, base64. With one set, an index that is not signed by it is refused. With none, the catalogue is still readable and every entry is shown as vouched for by nobody. Generate a pair with: skifity admin plugin-key

plugins_store_url.label: Plugin store
plugins_store_url.help: Where the panel looks for plugins. Leave empty for the Skifity store. Point it at your own index to run a store of your own, or clear the public key below to browse one that is not signed — a plugin can always be installed from a manifest address or by pasting one, which is what a cluster with no way out to the internet uses.

registry_password.label: Registry password
registry_password.help: A token with permission to push. Stored encrypted and never shown again.

registry_url.label: External registry
registry_url.help: Where built images are pushed. Leave empty to use the registry inside the cluster, which is the simplest option.

registry_username.label: Registry username
registry_username.help: Needed only for an external registry. The registry inside the cluster needs no credentials.

signin_oidc_allowed_domains.label: Allowed email domains
signin_oidc_allowed_domains.help: Comma-separated. Only people whose verified email is in one of these domains may sign in. Leave empty to accept anybody the provider vouches for, which is only safe when the provider is yours.

signin_oidc_auto_create.label: Create an account on first sign-in
signin_oidc_auto_create.help: With this off, somebody the provider knows and this panel does not is refused, so accounts are created by invitation rather than by anyone with a company address.

signin_oidc_button_label.label: Sign-in button text
signin_oidc_button_label.help: What the button on the sign-in page says. Leave empty for a generic label.

signin_oidc_client_id.label: Client ID
signin_oidc_client_id.help: From the application you registered with the provider. Its redirect URI is this panel's address followed by /api/auth/sso/callback.

signin_oidc_client_secret.label: Client secret
signin_oidc_client_secret.help: Stored encrypted and never shown again.

signin_oidc_issuer.label: Single sign-on issuer
signin_oidc_issuer.help: The OpenID Connect issuer URL of your identity provider — Okta, Entra, Authentik, Keycloak, Zitadel, Google. Skifity reads its configuration from /.well-known/openid-configuration under this address. Leave empty to sign in with a password only.

storage_s3_access_key.label: S3 access key
storage_s3_access_key.help: Use a key that can only write to this bucket.

storage_s3_bucket.label: S3 bucket
storage_s3_bucket.help: The bucket backups are written to. Skifity does not create it for you.

storage_s3_endpoint.label: S3 endpoint
storage_s3_endpoint.help: Any S3-compatible service works: AWS, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, or a MinIO server you run yourself.

storage_s3_path_style.label: Use path-style URLs
storage_s3_path_style.help: Turn this on for MinIO and most self-hosted S3 services.

storage_s3_region.label: S3 region
storage_s3_region.help: Some providers ignore this; AWS does not.

storage_s3_secret_key.label: S3 secret key
storage_s3_secret_key.help: Stored encrypted and never shown again.

storage_panel_backup_schedule.label: Back up this panel
storage_panel_backup_schedule.help: When to copy this panel's own database to the bucket above, as a cron schedule in UTC. Empty copies it every day at 03:17; off turns it off. The master key is never uploaded: keep it somewhere else, because a restore needs both.

storage_panel_backup_keep.label: Panel backups to keep
storage_panel_backup_keep.help: How many copies of this panel's database to keep in the bucket. Older ones are deleted after a new one succeeds, never before. Empty keeps 14.

signin_oidc_groups_claim.label: Groups claim
signin_oidc_groups_claim.help: The claim in the ID token that lists a person's groups. Empty is groups. The provider has to put it in the ID token.

signin_oidc_group_roles.label: Groups to teams
signin_oidc_group_roles.help: One per line: a group, then the team and the role it gives, as platform-admins = acme:admin. A team named here follows the groups at every single sign-on: a person gets the highest role their groups give, and leaves the team when none do. Teams not named here are left alone, and a team's last owner is never removed.

storage_backup_passphrase.label: Backup passphrase
storage_backup_passphrase.help: When set, every backup is encrypted with it before it leaves the cluster, so the bucket's owner cannot read it. Keep a copy somewhere else: a backup cannot be restored without it, and the panel cannot tell it to you again.

cluster_build_concurrency.label: Builds at once
cluster_build_concurrency.help: How many builds run at the same time. More wait their turn, in the order they came, and say so in their log. Each build can use up to 3 GiB of memory, taken from what the apps have.

signin_api_allowed_networks.label: API tokens only from
signin_api_allowed_networks.help: Addresses or networks, one per line, such as 203.0.113.7 or 10.0.0.0/8. When set, an API token — the CLI's, a CI job's, an assistant's — is refused from anywhere else, even though it is valid. Signing in to the panel in a browser is not affected. Empty lets tokens in from anywhere.

scanning_enabled.label: Scan images for known vulnerabilities
scanning_enabled.help: On by default. Every image an app runs is scanned with Trivy when it is built or deployed, and again on the schedule below, and each app's Security tab lists what was found. Trivy downloads its database of vulnerabilities from mirror.gcr.io or ghcr.io; on a cluster with no way out to the internet, turn this off. A scan never holds up a deploy unless the setting below says so.

scanning_schedule.label: Scan running apps again
scanning_schedule.help: When to scan the image every app runs again, as a cron schedule in UTC, because new vulnerabilities are published about images nobody has changed. Empty scans every day at 04:23; off leaves it to deploys and Scan now. Apps are scanned one at a time, and one scanned in the last twelve hours is skipped.

scanning_block_fixable_critical.label: Stop deploys with a critical vulnerability that has a fix
scanning_block_fixable_critical.help: Off by default. When on, a deploy waits for its image to be scanned and stops if a critical vulnerability in it has a fixed version, naming the packages and the versions to move to. Somebody can still deploy it by accepting the vulnerabilities, which is recorded in the activity log. A scan that cannot run lets the deploy through, and a rollback is never stopped.

settings.removeMemberConfirm: {{name}} loses access to this team and everything in it.
settings.revokeInvitationConfirm: The link sent to {{email}} stops working.
settings.panelBackupsHelp: Copies of this panel's own database — apps, teams, settings and history — in the bucket set under Backup storage, which is also where you say when and how many. Secrets stay sealed with the master key, and the key is never uploaded: keep it somewhere else.
settings.panelBackupsNone: No copies yet. Once backup storage is set, one is taken on schedule, or take one now.
settings.panelBackupTaken: A copy of this panel is in the bucket.
settings.panelBackupsRestore: To put one back, download it from the bucket to the server, stop the panel, and run:
settings.readOnly: You are a viewer in {{team}}: you can see its apps, deployments and logs, and anything you try to change will be refused. An admin of the team can give you more.
settings.noProjectsLeft: No projects: the ones they had were deleted
settings.limitToProjectsHelp: They see only the projects ticked below — not the others, the servers or the team's settings.
settings.memberAdded: They already had an account, so they were added to the team directly.
settings.requireStrongAuthHelp: Everybody in this team, owners included, has to sign in with a second factor or through single sign-on. A password alone sees nothing in the team, and neither does a token whose owner has neither.
settings.strongAuthNeeded: You signed in with a password alone, so nothing in this team is shown to you. Turn on two-factor authentication, or sign in with single sign-on.
settings.componentUpgradeConfirm: The manifest of version {{to}} is applied over {{from}}, which is how the project documents its own upgrade. The component restarts; your apps do not.
settings.componentVersionUnknown: the version installed before versions were recorded

errors.copiedForAI: Copied. Paste it into your AI assistant.
errors.crashHelp: Something in the panel could not be drawn. Your apps and servers are not affected — only this screen is. Try again, or go somewhere else in the panel.
errors.pageNotFoundHelp: The link may be old, or the thing it pointed at may have been deleted.
errors.offlineHelp: Your apps keep running. This page will reconnect on its own.

admin_backup_failed.title: The database could not be copied
admin_backup_failed.fix: Check that the directory exists, that the file does not, and that there is room on the disk.

admin_no_database.title: The panel's database is not here
admin_no_database.fix: Run this on the server the panel is installed on, as root. If the database is somewhere else, pass --database, or set SKIFITY_DATABASE_PATH.

admin_no_such_user.title: No account with that address
admin_no_such_user.fix: Run `{{0}} admin list-users` to see the accounts that do exist.

app_crash_loop.title: This app keeps restarting
app_crash_loop.cause: {{0}} has restarted {{1}} times in a row. Kubernetes is backing off between restarts.
app_crash_loop.impact: The app is not serving traffic reliably.
app_crash_loop.fix: Read the last log lines below: the cause is almost always in them. Missing environment variables, a database that is not reachable, and a port the app does not actually listen on are the usual three.

auth_csrf.title: This request was blocked for safety
auth_csrf.cause: The request did not carry a matching CSRF token.
auth_csrf.fix: Reload the page and try again. If you are calling the API directly, use an API token with an Authorization header instead of a cookie.

auth_forbidden.title: You do not have permission for this
auth_forbidden.cause: Your role in this team does not allow {{0}}.
auth_forbidden.fix: Ask a team owner or admin to do this, or to raise your role.

auth_invalid_credentials.title: Email or password is not correct
auth_invalid_credentials.cause: The email address and password do not match an account on this panel.
auth_invalid_credentials.fix: Check for typos and try again. After several failed attempts sign-in pauses for a while.

auth_invalid_totp.title: That code is not correct
auth_invalid_totp.cause: The six-digit code did not match the one this panel expects.
auth_invalid_totp.impact: Two-factor authentication was not turned on.
auth_invalid_totp.fix: Check that your phone's clock is correct, then type the current code from your authenticator app.

auth_rate_limited.title: Too many attempts
auth_rate_limited.cause: There have been too many failed sign-in attempts for this account or from this address.
auth_rate_limited.impact: Sign-in is paused so that passwords cannot be guessed.
auth_rate_limited.fix: Wait {{0}} and try again. If this was not you, change your password once you can sign in.

auth_required.title: You need to sign in
auth_required.cause: This request had no valid session or API token.
auth_required.fix: Sign in again. If you are using the CLI, run `skifity login`.

auth_token_scope.title: This token cannot make that request
auth_token_scope.impact: The request was refused. Nothing was changed.
auth_token_scope.fix: Use a token without a scope, or create one that can write, under Account.

backup_bad_schedule.title: That is not a schedule Skifity understands
backup_bad_schedule.fix: Use five cron fields, for example "0 3 * * *" for every day at 03:00 UTC.

backup_bucket_missing.title: That bucket does not exist
backup_bucket_missing.cause: The bucket {{0}} was not found at {{1}}.
backup_bucket_missing.fix: Create the bucket in your storage provider, then try again. Skifity does not create buckets: doing so would need broader permissions than writing backups.

backup_database_not_running.title: This database is not running
backup_database_not_running.cause: {{0}} is {{1}}, so there is nothing to back up.
backup_database_not_running.fix: Wait for the database to be running, then try again.

backup_failed.title: The backup failed
backup_failed.impact: There is no new backup from this run. Earlier backups are untouched.
backup_failed.fix: Check the storage credentials in Settings and that the bucket exists and is writable. Then run the backup again from the database page.

backup_restore_refused.title: This restore would overwrite live data
backup_restore_refused.cause: {{0}} is in use and the restore would replace its current contents.
backup_restore_refused.fix: Restore into a new database instead, check it, then point your app at it. If you really do mean to overwrite, confirm it explicitly on the restore dialog.

backup_storage_no_delete.title: Old backups cannot be removed
backup_storage_no_delete.cause: The access key can write to {{0}} but cannot delete from it.
backup_storage_no_delete.impact: Backups will work, but old ones will never be cleaned up and the bucket will grow forever.
backup_storage_no_delete.fix: Give the access key permission to delete objects, or set the retention policy in your storage provider instead.

backup_storage_not_configured.title: No backup storage is configured
backup_storage_not_configured.cause: This team has no S3-compatible storage set up yet.
backup_storage_not_configured.impact: Backups cannot run, so nothing is being kept safe.
backup_storage_not_configured.fix: Open Settings, then Storage, and add an S3-compatible bucket. Any provider works: AWS S3, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, or a MinIO server you run yourself.

backup_storage_read_only.title: The backup storage cannot be written to
backup_storage_read_only.cause: Writing a test object to {{0}} failed: {{1}}
backup_storage_read_only.fix: Give the access key permission to put objects in this bucket.

backup_storage_unreachable.title: The backup storage could not be reached
backup_storage_unreachable.fix: Check the endpoint, the access key and that this server can reach the storage service.

build_failed.title: The build failed
build_failed.impact: The new version was not deployed. The previous version is still running and still serving traffic.
build_failed.fix: Read the build log below. Then fix it in your repository and push again, or press Retry if you believe it was a transient failure.

build_no_builder.title: Skifity could not work out how to build this repository
build_no_builder.cause: No Dockerfile was found in {{0}}, and the files present do not match any language Skifity recognises.
build_no_builder.fix: Add a Dockerfile to the repository, or set the root directory if your app lives in a subfolder of a monorepo, or choose a prebuilt image instead.

build_pod_not_started.title: The build did not start
build_pod_not_started.cause: No build pod became ready within five minutes.
build_pod_not_started.fix: Check that the cluster has free CPU and memory, and that the builder component is running.

build_timeout.title: The build took too long and was stopped
build_timeout.cause: The build did not finish within 40 minutes.
build_timeout.impact: Nothing was deployed. The previous version is still running.

cluster_token_missing.cause: The panel is running in a Kubernetes cluster it did not create, and a server can only join that cluster with the token it was started with.

cluster_unreachable.title: The cluster is not responding

deploy_cannot_rollback.title: This version cannot be rolled back to

deploy_image_pull_failed.title: The image could not be pulled

deploy_image_pull_failed.fix: If this is a private image, add the registry credentials in Settings. If it is an internal build, the in-cluster registry may not be reachable from this node: check that the node joined the cluster network.

deploy_refused_by_plugin.impact: Nothing was changed. The version that was serving is still serving.

deploy_rollout_timeout.title: The new version did not start

The usual causes are a missing environment variable, a health check path that does not exist yet, a port mismatch between the app and the configured port, and an app that needs longer to start than its time to start under Settings allows.

detect_unreadable.title: That repository could not be read
detect_unreadable.impact: Nothing was created. You can still fill the form in yourself.
detect_unreadable.fix: Check the address and the branch. A private repository needs a connected Git account with access to it, chosen below.

firewall_failed.title: The firewall could not be configured

firewall_no_geo_database.fix: Turn on "Look up a visitor's country and network" under Settings, then Domains and HTTPS. It uses DB-IP's free monthly databases, which need no account.

guard_no_panel_image.title: The firewall could not be installed
guard_no_panel_image.cause: The panel's own Deployment could not be read, so there is no image to run the guard from: {{0}}
guard_no_panel_image.impact: Nothing was changed in the cluster.

plugin_bad_manifest.fix: Check it against the plugin standard, which is documented at /docs/plugins.

preflight_conflict_other.title: This server is not ready to join
preflight_conflict_other.impact: The server was not added. Nothing was changed on it.
preflight_conflict_other.fix: Check that it does not use ports 80, 443 or 6443.

preflight_conflict_web_server.impact: The server was not added. Nothing was changed on it.

preflight_cpu.title: This server is not ready to join
preflight_cpu.cause: This server has {{0}} CPU core(s); at least {{1}} is needed.
preflight_cpu.impact: The server was not added. Nothing was changed on it.
preflight_cpu.fix: Resize the server to one with more cores.

preflight_disk.title: This server is not ready to join

preflight_disk.impact: The server was not added. Nothing was changed on it.

preflight_memory_control_plane.impact: The server was not added. Nothing was changed on it.
preflight_memory_control_plane.fix: Resize the server, or add it as a worker rather than a control plane server.

preflight_memory_worker.cause: This server has {{0}} MB of memory; a worker needs at least {{1}} MB.
preflight_memory_worker.impact: The server was not added. Nothing was changed on it.
preflight_memory_worker.fix: Resize the server, or add it as a worker rather than a control plane server.

ssh_unreachable.title: Could not reach the server over SSH
ssh_unreachable.impact: The server was not added. Nothing was changed on it.
ssh_unreachable.fix: Check that the IP address and port are right, that the server is running, and that your provider's firewall allows inbound TCP on port {{0}}. Many providers block everything by default in their control panel, which SSH cannot open from here.

sso_no_panel_url.title: This panel does not know its own address
sso_no_panel_url.cause: Single sign-on sends people back to a fixed address, and the Panel URL setting is empty.
sso_no_panel_url.fix: Set the Panel URL under Settings, then register that address followed by /api/auth/sso/callback with your provider.

sso_not_configured.title: Single sign-on is not set up
sso_not_configured.cause: No identity provider is configured on this panel.
sso_not_configured.impact: Sign in with an email address and password instead.
sso_not_configured.fix: An administrator can configure a provider under Settings, Sign-in.

sso_provider_unreachable.title: The identity provider could not be reached
sso_provider_unreachable.impact: Nobody can sign in with single sign-on until this is fixed.
sso_provider_unreachable.fix: Check the issuer URL under Settings, Sign-in, and that this panel can reach it.

store_bad_index.title: The plugin store's index could not be read
store_bad_index.fix: If this is a store of your own, check that the index is the format this panel reads. A plugin can still be installed from a manifest address or by pasting one.

store_bad_signature.title: The plugin store's index is not signed by the key this panel trusts
store_bad_signature.impact: Nothing was read from it, and nothing was installed.
store_bad_signature.fix: Check the signing key under Settings, then Plugins. If it is right, the index at {{0}} is not the one that key signs, and that is worth finding out about before installing anything from it.

store_unreachable.title: The plugin store could not be reached
store_unreachable.fix: Check that this cluster can reach {{0}}. A plugin can still be installed from a manifest address or by pasting one, which is what a cluster with no way out to the internet uses.

team_account_exists.title: They already have an account here
team_account_exists.cause: {{0}} has signed in to this panel before, so there is nothing to sign up for.
team_account_exists.fix: Add them to the team under Members, by the same address.

team_already_a_member.title: They are already in this team
team_already_a_member.fix: Change their role under Members instead.

team_last_owner.title: A team needs at least one owner
team_last_owner.cause: This is the only owner of the team.
team_last_owner.fix: Make someone else an owner first, then remove this one.

team_no_such_user.title: No account with that email
team_no_such_user.cause: Nobody on this panel uses the address {{0}}.
team_no_such_user.impact: Nobody was added to the team.
team_no_such_user.fix: Ask them to create an account first, then add them. Skifity does not send invitations to addresses that have never signed in.

tunnel_no_token.title: There is no Cloudflare tunnel token
tunnel_no_token.cause: Settings has no tunnel token, and the connector cannot authenticate without one.
tunnel_no_token.impact: The tunnel was not installed. Nothing was changed in the cluster.
tunnel_no_token.fix: Create a tunnel in the Cloudflare dashboard under Zero Trust, then Networks, then Tunnels. Choose the Cloudflared connector, copy the token it shows, and paste it into Settings, then Domains and HTTPS, then Cloudflare tunnel token. On the same tunnel, add a public hostname — a wildcard such as *.apps.example.com covers every app at once — with the service set to HTTP and the address {{0}}.

tunnel_not_applied.title: The token was saved, but the tunnel was not updated
tunnel_not_applied.impact: The connectors are still running on the previous token, so traffic keeps flowing until they are restarted.
tunnel_not_applied.fix: Fix what the cause says and save the token again, or install Cloudflare tunnel under Components.

upgrade_failed.title: The upgrade could not be started
upgrade_failed.impact: The panel is still running the current version.
upgrade_failed.fix: Check that the version exists and that the cluster can pull its image.

upgrade_unsupported.title: This panel cannot upgrade itself
upgrade_unsupported.cause: The panel is not running inside a cluster it can update, which is normal in development.
upgrade_unsupported.fix: Upgrade by pulling the new image and restarting, or re-run the installer with the version you want.

webhook_unverified.title: This webhook could not be verified
webhook_unverified.cause: The signature on the request does not match this connection's webhook secret.
webhook_unverified.fix: Check that the secret in your Git host's webhook settings matches the one in Skifity.

auth_reauth_required.title: Confirm it is you
auth_reauth_required.cause: This action needs your password again, because holding a signed-in session is not the same as being at the keyboard.

auth_reauth_failed.title: That is not the right password
auth_reauth_failed.cause: The password, or the two-factor code, did not match this account.
auth_reauth_failed.fix: Type it again. After several wrong attempts this pauses for a while.

auth_no_password.title: This account has no password to confirm with
auth_no_password.cause: It signs in through your identity provider, and two-factor authentication is not turned on here, so there is nothing this panel can ask you for.
auth_no_password.fix: Turn on two-factor authentication for this account first, or use an account with a password.

auth_needs_person.title: This has to be done from the panel
auth_needs_person.cause: Changing two-factor authentication or creating a token has to be done by somebody who can prove who they are, and an API token cannot.
auth_needs_person.fix: Sign in to the panel and do it there.

cli_app_not_created.title: The panel did not say which app it created
cli_app_not_created.cause: The reply to creating an app had no app in it.
cli_app_not_created.impact: The project file was not written, so `skifity deploy` here would not know what to deploy.
cli_app_not_created.fix: Find it with `skifity apps`, and put its id in skifity.toml as app = "<id>".

upload_none.title: There is no code to deploy yet
upload_none.cause: {{0}} deploys a folder from somebody's computer, and nothing has been sent yet.
upload_none.fix: Press Send a new version on the app's page and pick its folder, or run `skifity up` in the folder.

upload_not_found.title: That upload is not on the panel
upload_not_found.cause: No upload with the hash {{0}} belongs to this app. The panel keeps each app's ten newest uploads.
upload_not_found.fix: Send the folder again, from the app's page or with `skifity up`.

upload_not_an_archive.title: The panel could not read this upload
upload_not_an_archive.cause: What was sent is not a whole gzipped tar archive.
upload_not_an_archive.impact: Nothing was stored, built or deployed.
upload_not_an_archive.fix: Send the folder with `skifity up`, which packs it the way the panel reads it. If you did, the transfer was probably cut off, so run it again.

upload_unsafe_entry.title: The upload has a file the panel will not unpack
upload_unsafe_entry.cause: {{0}} is a link, a special file or a path that leads outside the folder, and unpacking it could write somewhere it should not.
upload_unsafe_entry.impact: Nothing was stored, built or deployed.
upload_unsafe_entry.fix: Remove it from the folder, or list it in .skifityignore so it is not sent.

upload_secrets_file.title: The upload has a .env file in it
upload_secrets_file.cause: {{0}} holds the app's real settings. A build puts every file it is given into the image, where anyone who can pull the image could read them.
upload_secrets_file.impact: Nothing was stored, built or deployed.
upload_secrets_file.fix: Set those values under the app's Variables instead. `skifity up` leaves .env files out by itself, so this one was sent some other way.

upload_too_many_files.title: The upload has too many files
upload_too_many_files.cause: It holds more than {{0}} files, which source code almost never does.
upload_too_many_files.impact: Nothing was stored, built or deployed.
upload_too_many_files.fix: A dependency folder such as node_modules or a virtualenv is probably in it. List it in .skifityignore: the build installs dependencies itself.

upload_unpacks_too_large.title: The upload is too large once unpacked
upload_unpacks_too_large.cause: Its contents add up to more than {{0}} MB.
upload_unpacks_too_large.impact: Nothing was stored, built or deployed.
upload_unpacks_too_large.fix: Build output, a dependency folder or a data file is probably in it. List it in .skifityignore and send it again.

upload_empty.title: The upload has no files in it
upload_empty.cause: The archive was read to the end and held folders at most.
upload_empty.impact: Nothing was stored, built or deployed.
upload_empty.fix: Run `skifity up` from inside the app's folder, or name the folder: `skifity up ./my-app`.

upload_too_large.title: The upload is too large
upload_too_large.cause: The panel accepts up to {{0}} MB of compressed code, and this was more.
upload_too_large.impact: Nothing was stored, built or deployed.
upload_too_large.fix: Something that is not source code is probably in the folder, such as a dependency folder, build output or a database file. Add it to .skifityignore and send it again.

upload_wrong_source.title: This app does not deploy uploaded code
upload_wrong_source.cause: {{0}} builds from a repository or an image, so code sent to it would never be used.
upload_wrong_source.fix: Push to the repository instead, or create a new app for the folder with `skifity up --new`.

upload_delivery_failed.title: The code could not be handed to the build
upload_delivery_failed.cause: The panel could not send the uploaded code into the build: {{0}}
upload_delivery_failed.impact: Nothing was built or deployed. The previous version is still running.
upload_delivery_failed.fix: Press Retry. If it fails again, check that the panel can reach the cluster's API and that the build pod started.

cli_platform_unknown.title: There is no command line tool for that platform
cli_platform_unknown.cause: {{0}} is not a platform the command line tool is built for. It is built for linux, darwin (macOS) and windows, on amd64 and arm64.
cli_platform_unknown.fix: Ask for one of those, for example ?os=darwin&arch=arm64 for a Mac with Apple silicon.

cli_platform_unavailable.title: This panel does not have the command line tool for that platform
cli_platform_unavailable.cause: There is no build for {{0}} beside this panel. It has: {{1}}.
cli_platform_unavailable.impact: Nothing was downloaded. Deploying a folder from the panel's own New app page works without it.
