api_description_unreadable.title: The API description could not be read
api_description_unreadable.cause: The OpenAPI description built into this panel is not valid YAML: {{0}}
api_description_unreadable.impact: Only the description is missing. Every route it describes works as before.
api_description_unreadable.fix: This build of Skifity is faulty. Report it with the version /api/meta names; the routes are also listed in llms.txt.

sso_last_way_in.title: Single sign-on is this account's only way in
sso_last_way_in.cause: This account has no password, so unlinking the provider would leave it with no way to sign in.
sso_last_way_in.fix: Set a password on this page first, then unlink.

build_nixpacks_unavailable.title: Nixpacks is not available
build_nixpacks_unavailable.cause: {{0}} is set to build with Nixpacks. Its makers replaced it with Railpack, and its command line is not published as an image a build can run.
build_nixpacks_unavailable.fix: Set the app's builder to Automatic, which uses Railpack, or to Dockerfile, under the app's Settings.

provision_cluster_version_unknown.title: Could not find out which Kubernetes version the cluster runs
provision_cluster_version_unknown.impact: The server was not joined. A server has to run the same version as the cluster it joins.
provision_cluster_version_unknown.fix: Check that the panel can reach the Kubernetes API, then retry.

admin_restore_unreadable.title: That backup could not be read
admin_restore_unreadable.fix: Give the file exactly as it came out of the bucket: a .db.gz, or a .db from `{{0}} admin backup-db`.

admin_restore_not_a_panel.title: That is not a whole panel database
admin_restore_not_a_panel.fix: Take a different backup. The newest one in the bucket's skifity/panel/ folder is usually the one to use.

auth_scoped_to_projects.title: Your access is limited to some projects
auth_scoped_to_projects.cause: You are in this team for some of its projects only, and this belongs to the whole team.
auth_scoped_to_projects.fix: Ask an admin of the team for access to the whole team, if you need this.

mcp_token_required.title: The MCP endpoint takes an API token
mcp_token_required.cause: This request was signed in with a browser session rather than an API token.
mcp_token_required.fix: Create a token under Account, then give it to the assistant as an Authorization: Bearer header.

store_schema_newer.title: This database belongs to a newer version
store_schema_newer.cause: The database has been migrated to schema {{0}}, and this version knows schema {{1}} at most.
store_schema_newer.impact: Nothing was read or changed. An older version writing to a newer database is how data is lost without anybody noticing.
store_schema_newer.fix: Run the version that upgraded it. To go back to this version instead, restore the copy taken before the upgrade with `{{0}} admin restore-db`.

upgrade_no_snapshot.title: The database could not be copied before upgrading
upgrade_no_snapshot.impact: The upgrade was not started. The panel is still running the current version.
upgrade_no_snapshot.fix: Make room on the disk the database is on, then upgrade again.

auth_strong_auth_required.title: This team asks for two-factor authentication
auth_strong_auth_required.cause: Everybody in this team has to sign in with a second factor or with single sign-on, and this sign-in used neither.
auth_strong_auth_required.impact: Nothing in the team was shown or changed.
auth_strong_auth_required.fix: Turn on two-factor authentication under Account, or sign in with single sign-on.

team_strong_auth_self.title: Turn on two-factor for yourself first
team_strong_auth_self.cause: This team is about to require a second factor or single sign-on, and you signed in with neither.
team_strong_auth_self.impact: Nothing was changed. Turning it on now would have locked you out of this team.
team_strong_auth_self.fix: Turn on two-factor authentication under Account, or sign in with single sign-on, then turn this on.

deploy_locked.title: Deploys to this app are locked
deploy_locked.impact: Nothing was deployed. The version running now keeps running.
deploy_locked.fix: Unlock deploys on the app's page, or with `{{0}} unlock`, once what they were locked for is over.

app_watch_path_invalid.title: That is not a path the app can watch
app_watch_path_invalid.cause: {{0}} is not a path or a pattern.
app_watch_path_invalid.fix: Write one path or pattern per line, starting at the repository's root: apps/web, apps/**/package.json, or !**/*.md to leave something out. A path cannot use .. to leave the repository.

app_too_many_watch_paths.title: That is too many paths to watch
app_too_many_watch_paths.cause: An app can watch at most {{0}} paths or patterns.
app_too_many_watch_paths.fix: Use a pattern that covers several paths at once, such as apps/** or packages/*/src.

app_maintenance_message.title: Write the message visitors will read
app_maintenance_message.cause: The maintenance page shows the message and nothing else, so it cannot be empty or longer than {{0}} characters.
app_maintenance_message.impact: Nothing was changed. The app is not in maintenance.
app_maintenance_message.fix: Write a sentence or two in the language your visitors read: what is happening, and when the app is back.

app_maintenance_address.title: That is not an address to let through
app_maintenance_address.cause: {{0}} is not an address or a range, or there are more than {{1}} of them.
app_maintenance_address.impact: Nothing was changed. The app is not in maintenance.
app_maintenance_address.fix: Write one address, like 203.0.113.7, or one range, like 203.0.113.0/24, per line.

app_maintenance_no_domain.title: This app has no address to show a page at
app_maintenance_no_domain.cause: Maintenance is a page shown at the app's domains, and this app has none.
app_maintenance_no_domain.fix: Add a domain on the Domains tab first. An app with no address has no visitors to show a page to.

stack_size.title: That is not a stack Skifity can create
stack_size.cause: A stack has between 1 and {{0}} services.
stack_size.fix: Pick the services to create. For a larger file, create it in parts in the same environment; the parts still reach each other by name.

stack_needs_repository.title: A service is built from a repository nobody named
stack_needs_repository.cause: The service {{0}} is built from source, and the stack has no repository to build it from.
stack_needs_repository.fix: Paste the repository's address first, then create the stack.

stack_no_source.title: A service has nothing to run
stack_no_source.cause: The service {{0}} has neither an image nor a build.
stack_no_source.fix: Give it an image or a build in the Compose file, or leave it out of the stack.

stack_duplicate.title: Two services would have the same name
stack_duplicate.cause: {{0}} and {{1}} both become {{2}}, and an environment has one app by each name.
stack_duplicate.fix: Rename one of them in the Compose file.

template_gone.title: There is no template version to update to
template_gone.cause: {{0}} did not come from a template this panel still has.
template_gone.fix: Change the image under Settings yourself if a newer version exists.

template_up_to_date.title: This app is already on the template's version
template_up_to_date.cause: {{0}} runs {{1}}, which is what the template sets.
template_up_to_date.fix: Updates arrive with new versions of the panel.

template_changed_by_hand.title: The image was changed by hand
template_changed_by_hand.cause: The app runs {{0}}, and the template last set {{1}}: somebody chose that image, and an update would replace it.
template_changed_by_hand.fix: Update anyway to go back to the template's version, or keep the image you chose.

template_update_running.title: An update is already under way
template_update_running.cause: {{0}} is being backed up before an update.
template_update_running.fix: Wait for it: the app page says when it has deployed or why it stopped.

template_needs_backups.title: There is nowhere to back up to first
template_needs_backups.cause: {{0}} has disks or databases, and an update backs them up before it starts, but backups are not configured.
template_needs_backups.fix: Set up backup storage under Settings, or update without a backup if you have one of your own.

promote_built_differently.title: This app would build that version differently
promote_built_differently.cause: The image was built with other build settings or build-time variables than {{0}} has, so it would run code built for the other environment.
promote_built_differently.fix: Make the build-time variables match, promote anyway to run the image as it was built, or deploy here to build it with this app's own.

promote_not_possible.title: That version cannot be promoted here
promote_not_possible.fix: Promote between the same app in two environments of one project, from a version that deployed.

backup_passphrase_missing.title: This backup is sealed, and there is no passphrase to open it
backup_passphrase_missing.cause: The backup was encrypted with the backup passphrase, and none is set now.
backup_passphrase_missing.fix: Enter the passphrase it was sealed with under Settings, then Storage, and restore again.

backup_wrong_passphrase.title: The backup passphrase does not open this backup
backup_wrong_passphrase.cause: This backup was sealed with a different passphrase than the one set now.
backup_wrong_passphrase.fix: Set the passphrase it was sealed with under Settings, then Storage, restore, and set the current one back.

backup_damaged.title: This backup is damaged
backup_damaged.fix: Restore an earlier backup, and check the storage the damaged one is in.

database_tunnel_unreachable.title: The panel could not reach this database
database_tunnel_unreachable.cause: {{0}} did not answer the panel, so there is nothing to tunnel to.
database_tunnel_unreachable.fix: Check the database is running on its page; one that is starting answers within a minute.

cli_no_database.title: There is no database here
cli_no_database.cause: This environment has no managed databases.
cli_no_database.fix: Add one in the panel under Databases, or pass --env for another environment.

cli_unknown_database.title: There is no database by that name
cli_unknown_database.cause: Nothing in this environment is called {{0}}.

cli_port_in_use.title: That port is taken
cli_port_in_use.cause: Port {{0}} on this computer could not be listened on: {{1}}.
cli_port_in_use.fix: Pass another --port, or leave it out to take any free one.

cli_tunnel_refused.title: The panel did not open a tunnel
cli_tunnel_refused.cause: It answered {{0}} to a request for one.
cli_tunnel_refused.fix: Something between here and the panel may not pass upgraded connections through; a panel reached directly does.

process_name_invalid.title: That cannot be a process's name
process_name_invalid.cause: {{0}} is not a lowercase name of up to 20 letters, digits and hyphens, or it is web or release, which an app already has.
process_name_invalid.fix: Use the name from the Procfile, such as worker or clock.

process_too_many.title: This app has as many processes as it can
process_too_many.cause: An app runs at most {{0}} processes beside web.
process_too_many.fix: Remove one it no longer needs, or make the rest a separate app from the same repository.

blueprint_invalid.title: skifity.yaml cannot be applied
blueprint_invalid.fix: Correct the file and run `skifity plan` again.

cli_no_blueprint.title: There is no skifity.yaml here
cli_no_blueprint.cause: Neither this directory nor any above it has one.
cli_no_blueprint.fix: Write one — the documentation's example is a start — or pass --file.

k3s_upgrade_blocked.title: k3s cannot be upgraded yet
k3s_upgrade_blocked.impact: Nothing was changed; every server runs the version it did.
k3s_upgrade_blocked.fix: Deal with each reason and check the plan again.

backup_no_panel_image.title: A sealed backup cannot be made or opened here
backup_no_panel_image.cause: Sealing runs the panel's own image in the backup job, and the panel's Deployment could not be read to find it: {{0}}
backup_no_panel_image.impact: Nothing was backed up, restored or changed, and nothing went to the bucket unencrypted.
backup_no_panel_image.fix: This works when the panel runs inside the cluster it manages, as the installer sets it up. A panel outside it can back up only without a passphrase, which sends backups unencrypted.

plugin_manifest_changed.title: That manifest is not the one the store signed
plugin_manifest_changed.cause: The store listed a manifest with the digest {{0}}, and the file at {{1}} now has the digest {{2}}.
plugin_manifest_changed.fix: Tell the store's publisher; install it from the store again once the two agree.

database_variable_taken.title: That variable already connects another database
database_variable_taken.cause: This app's {{0}} is the connection string of another database linked to it.
database_variable_taken.fix: Link this database under another name, or unlink the other one first.

run_outcome_unknown.title: How the command ended could not be read
run_outcome_unknown.cause: Its output ended, and the panel could not read its exit status: {{0}} is still running, or its pod is gone.
run_outcome_unknown.impact: It may have succeeded or failed; the output above is all there is.
run_outcome_unknown.fix: Look at the app's Console tab, or run it again.

cli_explain_unknown.title: There is no error with that code to explain
cli_explain_unknown.cause: The last error this CLI printed is not {{0}}.
cli_explain_unknown.fix: Run the command again, then `{{0}} status --explain` with the code it prints. An error in the panel has a "Copy error for AI" button in Activity.

cli_project_ambiguous.title: Which project is not clear
cli_project_ambiguous.cause: There is no {{0}} here, and the team has {{1}} projects: {{2}}.
cli_project_ambiguous.fix: Run the command where the app's {{0}} is, name the app with --app, or name the environment with --env.

cli_environment_ambiguous.title: Which environment is not clear
cli_environment_ambiguous.cause: The project has no production environment, and {{0}} others: {{1}}.
cli_environment_ambiguous.fix: Run the command where the app's {{0}} is, name the app with --app, or name the environment with --env.

cli_wrong_panel.title: This folder's app is on another panel
cli_wrong_panel.cause: {{0}} says the app is on {{1}}, and you are signed in to {{2}}.
cli_wrong_panel.fix: Sign in to {{0}} with `{{1}} login`, or set SKIFITY_URL and SKIFITY_TOKEN for it.

network.title: The panel could not be reached
network.impact: The page may be showing stale information.
network.fix: Check your connection and reload. If the panel is restarting, this clears up on its own.

unexpected.title: Something went wrong
unexpected.impact: The action may not have completed.
unexpected.fix: Try again. If it keeps happening, copy this and open an issue.

file_too_large.title: That is more than an app's files can hold
file_too_large.cause: An app's files are configuration, kept together in one place that holds at most {{0}} KiB.
file_too_large.fix: Put data in a volume, or build it into the image, and keep files for configuration.

file_too_many.title: This app has as many files as it can
file_too_many.cause: An app has at most {{0}} files.
file_too_many.fix: Remove one it no longer needs, or put several settings in one file.

registry_login_refused.title: The registry turned these credentials down
registry_login_refused.cause: {{0}} answered that this username and password cannot sign in.
registry_login_refused.impact: The credentials were not saved, so nothing will pull with them.
registry_login_refused.fix: Check the username, and use a token with permission to read packages — ghcr.io and Docker Hub want a token in place of the account's password.

port_taken.title: That port is already open for another app
port_taken.cause: {{0}}/{{1}} is open on every server already, for another app on this panel.
port_taken.fix: Choose another public port: the app can still listen on its own, and only the public side changes.

app_deploy_trigger_invalid.title: An app deploys on a branch or on a tag
app_deploy_trigger_invalid.cause: {{0}} is not something an app can deploy on.
app_deploy_trigger_invalid.fix: Use branch to deploy every push to the app's branch, or tag to deploy only the tags whose name matches its tag pattern.

app_tag_pattern_invalid.title: That is not a tag pattern
app_tag_pattern_invalid.cause: {{0}} is not a pattern a tag's name can be matched against.
app_tag_pattern_invalid.fix: Write one pattern of up to 100 characters, such as v* or release-*: * matches any run of characters except a slash, ? matches one character, and [0-9] one of a set. Close every [ you open.

git_listing_unsupported.title: This Git connection cannot list repositories
git_listing_unsupported.cause: {{0}} is a plain Git connection: it has a token and no API the panel knows how to ask.
git_listing_unsupported.impact: Nothing was listed. Apps can still be created from it.
git_listing_unsupported.fix: Type the repository's address and its branch into the form.

git_listing_failed.title: The Git host did not list what it has
git_listing_failed.impact: Nothing was listed. You can still type the repository's address and branch yourself.
git_listing_failed.fix: Check that the connection's token can read repositories — the repo scope or Contents read access on GitHub, read_api on GitLab, read:repository on Gitea, read:repository:bitbucket on Bitbucket — and that the panel can reach the Git host.

auth_reset_unavailable.title: This panel cannot send a reset link
auth_reset_unavailable.cause: It has no mail server set, or no Panel URL to link to.
auth_reset_unavailable.fix: Ask an administrator of this panel to reset your password, or to fill in Settings → Email and the Panel URL. Whoever runs the server can also use skifity admin reset-password.

auth_reset_invalid.title: This reset link cannot be used
auth_reset_invalid.cause: It has been used already, it is more than 30 minutes old, or it was never a link this panel sent.
auth_reset_invalid.fix: Ask for a new link from the sign-in page. Only the newest one works.

app_health_check_unknown.title: That is not a health check
app_health_check_unknown.cause: {{0}} is not a way to check an app. It is http, tcp or none.
app_health_check_unknown.fix: Choose http to ask the app's health path, tcp to check that its port is open, or none for software that answers neither.

app_health_path_required.title: An HTTP health check needs a path
app_health_path_required.cause: The health check is set to HTTP, which asks the app a path, and there is no path to ask.
app_health_path_required.fix: Enter a path that returns 200 once the app is ready, such as /healthz, or choose TCP to check only that the port is open.

app_health_start_out_of_range.title: That is not a time an app can be given to start
app_health_start_out_of_range.cause: The time to start has to be from {{0}} to {{1}} seconds, and it is {{2}}.
app_health_start_out_of_range.fix: Give the app as long as its slowest start takes, with some room: two minutes suits most apps, and five to ten a JVM or an image that migrates its database before it listens.

app_health_timeout_out_of_range.title: That is not a time a health check can wait
app_health_timeout_out_of_range.cause: A health check can wait from {{0}} to {{1}} seconds for an answer, and this one is set to {{2}}.
app_health_timeout_out_of_range.fix: Three seconds suits most apps. Raise it only for a health path that does real work, such as checking the database, and keep that work quick.

domain_dns_lookup_failed.title: The DNS check did not get an answer
domain_dns_lookup_failed.cause: Looking up {{0}} did not finish: the DNS server the panel asks timed out or refused.
domain_dns_lookup_failed.impact: Nothing was changed. The domain is still attached, and whether it points here is not known yet.
domain_dns_lookup_failed.fix: Try again in a minute. If it keeps failing, check {{0}} from your own computer with `dig +short {{1}}`; a panel whose server cannot resolve names at all has a DNS problem of its own.

server_ssh_failed.title: Could not sign in to this server
server_ssh_failed.cause: Signing in to {{server}} over SSH with the key Skifity installed on it did not work.
server_ssh_failed.impact: Nothing was checked or changed on the server. It keeps running, and so do its apps.
server_ssh_failed.fix: Check that the server is up and that SSH is reachable from the panel. If somebody removed Skifity's key from ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, add it back, or remove the server and add it again.

server_ssh_hardening_refused.title: SSH passwords were not turned off
server_ssh_hardening_refused.cause: The change could not be confirmed on {{server}}, so it was undone.
server_ssh_hardening_refused.impact: SSH on the server is as it was: nothing was changed.
server_ssh_hardening_refused.fix: Set PasswordAuthentication no and KbdInteractiveAuthentication no in /etc/ssh/sshd_config on the server by hand, check it with sshd -t, and reload ssh.

auth_token_network.title: API tokens are not accepted from this address
auth_token_network.cause: This request came from {{ip}}, which is not on the list of networks API tokens may be used from.
auth_token_network.impact: The request was refused. The token itself is still valid.
auth_token_network.fix: Make the request from an address on the list, or ask a panel administrator to add this one under Settings, Sign-in.

backup_not_offered.title: Skifity does not back up this kind of database
backup_not_offered.cause: {{0}} runs {{1}}, which Skifity does not back up.
backup_not_offered.fix: Keep data you cannot lose in a database that is backed up, such as PostgreSQL, or copy it with the engine's own tools through `{{0}} db connect`.

deploy_vulnerable.title: This image has critical vulnerabilities that have a fix
deploy_vulnerable.cause: {{0}} critical vulnerabilities in the image of {{1}} have a fixed version: {{2}}.
deploy_vulnerable.impact: Nothing was deployed. The version running now keeps running.
deploy_vulnerable.fix: Move to the fixed versions — usually a newer base image or dependency — and deploy again. To deploy this image anyway, deploy it with the vulnerabilities accepted: Deploy anyway on the stopped deployment, or `{{0}} deploy --accept-vulnerabilities`. That is recorded in the activity log.

scan_database_unavailable.title: The vulnerability database could not be downloaded
scan_database_unavailable.cause: The scanner could not fetch its database: {{0}}
scan_database_unavailable.impact: This image was not scanned. Deploys are never held up by a scan that could not run.
scan_database_unavailable.fix: The cluster needs to reach mirror.gcr.io or ghcr.io over HTTPS, where the database is published. On a cluster with no way out to the internet, turn scanning off under Settings, Image scanning.

scan_pull_failed.title: The scanner could not read the image
scan_pull_failed.impact: This image was not scanned. The app is not affected.
scan_pull_failed.fix: For an image in a private registry, add the registry's credentials under Settings, Git, Private registries. For an image the panel built, deploy the app again: the registry keeps the last ten images of an app.

scan_timeout.title: The scan took too long and was stopped
scan_timeout.cause: Scanning {{0}} did not finish within fifteen minutes.
scan_timeout.impact: This image was not scanned. The app is not affected.
scan_timeout.fix: A very large image, or a slow way out to the internet the first time the database is downloaded, can take this long. Scan it again: the database is kept, so a second scan is quicker.

scan_failed.title: The image could not be scanned
scan_failed.impact: This image was not scanned. The app is not affected, and deploys are never held up by it.
scan_failed.fix: Scan it again. If it fails the same way, copy this error and open an issue.

scan_report_unreadable.title: The scan's report could not be read
scan_report_unreadable.cause: The scanner finished, and what it printed was not a report the panel can read: {{0}}
scan_report_unreadable.impact: Nothing was recorded for this scan. The app is not affected.
scan_report_unreadable.fix: Scan it again. If it keeps happening, copy this error and open an issue: it is a bug in Skifity.

scan_interrupted.title: The panel restarted during this scan
scan_interrupted.cause: The scan was queued or running when the panel stopped.
scan_interrupted.impact: This image was not scanned this time. The app is not affected.
scan_interrupted.fix: Scan it again with Scan now, or wait for the next scheduled scan.

scan_disabled.title: Image scanning is switched off
scan_disabled.cause: An administrator turned vulnerability scanning off for this panel.
scan_disabled.fix: Turn it on under Settings, Image scanning.

scan_no_image.title: This app has no image to scan yet
scan_no_image.cause: {{0}} has not been deployed, so there is no image to look at.
scan_no_image.fix: Deploy it. Its image is scanned once it is built.

cli_scan_wait.title: The scan has not finished yet
cli_scan_wait.cause: It was still queued or running after {{0}} minutes.
cli_scan_wait.impact: Nothing is wrong with the app. The scan carries on in the panel.
cli_scan_wait.fix: Run `{{0}} scan` later to read its report.

drift_check_failed.title: The app could not be compared with what the panel applies
drift_check_failed.impact: Nothing was changed. Whether anybody changed the app outside the panel is not known until this works.
drift_check_failed.fix: Check that the panel's service account can still read the app's namespace; somebody may have changed its permissions. If the cluster was just upgraded, try again in a minute.

events_unreadable.title: The cluster's events could not be read
events_unreadable.impact: Nothing was changed, and the app keeps running. Only this list is missing.
events_unreadable.fix: Check that the panel's service account can still list events and pods in that namespace. If the cluster was just upgraded, try again in a minute.

certificate_unreadable.title: That is not a certificate the panel can read
certificate_unreadable.cause: The certificate box holds no PEM certificate that could be read: {{0}}.
certificate_unreadable.fix: Paste the certificate file's contents, from -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- to -----END CERTIFICATE-----, followed by the intermediate certificates your certificate authority gave you. A .crt or .cer file in DER form converts with `openssl x509 -inform der -in cert.cer -out cert.pem`.

certificate_key_unreadable.title: That is not a private key the panel can read
certificate_key_unreadable.cause: The private key box holds no unencrypted PEM private key.
certificate_key_unreadable.fix: Paste the key that begins with -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----, -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY----- or -----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----. A key protected by a passphrase has to be decrypted first: `openssl pkey -in encrypted.key -out plain.key`.

certificate_key_mismatch.title: The private key does not belong to this certificate
certificate_key_mismatch.cause: The private key is not the one {{0}} was issued for.
certificate_key_mismatch.impact: Nothing was saved. Served together, every visitor's connection would fail.
certificate_key_mismatch.fix: Use the key the certificate request was made with. `openssl x509 -noout -pubkey -in cert.pem` and `openssl pkey -pubout -in key.pem` print the same thing for a key and certificate that belong together.

certificate_chain_broken.title: These certificates are not one chain
certificate_chain_broken.cause: {{0}} did not sign {{1}} or any certificate above it, so it is not part of its chain.
certificate_chain_broken.impact: Nothing was saved. The order does not matter, and was put right when that was all that was wrong.
certificate_chain_broken.fix: Paste your certificate and the intermediate certificates your certificate authority gave you for it, and nothing else — not another site's certificate, not an old intermediate.

certificate_expired.title: This certificate has expired
certificate_expired.cause: The certificate for {{0}} stopped being valid on {{1}}.
certificate_expired.impact: Nothing was saved. Every browser refuses an expired certificate.
certificate_expired.fix: Renew it with your certificate authority and upload the new one under the same name.

certificate_not_yet_valid.title: This certificate is not valid yet
certificate_not_yet_valid.cause: The certificate for {{0}} is valid from {{1}}.
certificate_not_yet_valid.impact: Nothing was saved. Served now, every browser would refuse it.
certificate_not_yet_valid.fix: Upload it once its validity has started. If the date looks wrong, check the clock on the server the panel runs on.

certificate_weak_key.title: This certificate's key is not strong enough
certificate_weak_key.cause: The key is {{0}}. The panel serves RSA keys of 2048 bits or more, ECDSA keys on P-256 or P-384, and Ed25519 keys.
certificate_weak_key.fix: Make a new key and certificate request, for example `openssl req -new -newkey rsa:3072 -nodes -keyout key.pem -out request.csr`, and have it issued again.

certificate_no_hostnames.title: This certificate names no hostname
certificate_no_hostnames.cause: The certificate for {{0}} has no DNS names in its Subject Alternative Name, and browsers stopped reading the Common Name years ago.
certificate_no_hostnames.impact: Nothing was saved. It would match none of your domains.
certificate_no_hostnames.fix: Have it issued again with the hostnames as Subject Alternative Names, such as DNS:shop.example.com or DNS:*.example.com.

certificate_hostname_taken.title: This certificate names a hostname that is not this team's
certificate_hostname_taken.cause: {{0}} is this panel's own address, another team's domain, or named by another team's certificate.
certificate_hostname_taken.impact: Nothing was saved. The ingress serves certificates by name for the whole cluster, so this one would be sent to visitors of that hostname too.
certificate_hostname_taken.fix: Use a certificate that names only this team's hostnames. If the hostname is yours, remove it from where it is used first.

domain_named_by_certificate.title: Another team's certificate names this hostname
domain_named_by_certificate.cause: {{0}} is named in a certificate another team on this panel uploaded.
domain_named_by_certificate.impact: The domain was not added. Both certificates would be served for it, in whatever order the ingress read them.
domain_named_by_certificate.fix: Ask the panel's administrator which team uses the hostname. A certificate is removed under Settings, Certificates.

git_bitbucket_token_refused.title: Bitbucket did not accept this token
git_bitbucket_token_refused.cause: Bitbucket answered {{0}} when the panel asked what the token can read.
git_bitbucket_token_refused.fix: Use an API token with read:repository:bitbucket and read:workspace:bitbucket, with the Atlassian account's email or with none; or an access token with Repositories read, with its workspace named. App passwords no longer work.

git_bitbucket_workspace_unknown.title: Bitbucket has no such workspace for this token
git_bitbucket_workspace_unknown.cause: Bitbucket answered that there is no workspace {{0}} this token can read.
git_bitbucket_workspace_unknown.fix: Give the workspace's id, the part of a repository's address after bitbucket.org/, or leave it empty to use every workspace an API token can see.

git_bitbucket_check_failed.title: Bitbucket could not be asked about this token
git_bitbucket_check_failed.fix: Check that this server can reach api.bitbucket.org over HTTPS, then try again.

template_catalogue_address.title: That address cannot be a template catalogue
template_catalogue_address.fix: Give the https address of a YAML or JSON index of templates, or of a .tar.gz or .zip of them. A token for a private Git host goes in the header, where it is sealed, and not in the address.

template_catalogue_header.title: That header cannot be sent with the catalogue's download
template_catalogue_header.fix: Name the header the Git host reads a token from — Authorization, or PRIVATE-TOKEN for GitLab — and give its whole value, such as Bearer followed by the token.

template_catalogue_fetch_failed.title: The catalogue could not be downloaded
template_catalogue_fetch_failed.cause: {{0}} did not answer with a catalogue: {{1}}
template_catalogue_fetch_failed.impact: Nothing was saved: a catalogue is kept once it has been downloaded and read.
template_catalogue_fetch_failed.fix: Open the address in a browser, check the header for a private host, and check this server can reach it. An address on this machine or the cloud's metadata service is refused on purpose, and so is a redirect to a private address.

template_catalogue_unreadable.title: That is not a template catalogue
template_catalogue_unreadable.cause: What {{0}} answered could not be read: {{1}}
template_catalogue_unreadable.fix: Point it at a YAML or JSON file with a list of templates under templates:, or at a .tar.gz or .zip of *.yaml files in the same schema as the built-in catalogue. A raw file's address, not the page that shows it.

template_catalogue_refresh_failed.title: The catalogue could not be refreshed
template_catalogue_refresh_failed.cause: {{0}} could not be downloaded or read again: {{1}}
template_catalogue_refresh_failed.impact: Its templates are still installed from the copy downloaded before, which was kept.
template_catalogue_refresh_failed.fix: Check the address still answers with the catalogue and the header is still valid, then refresh it again. It is also tried again every day.

template_catalogue_limit.title: This team has as many catalogues as it can
template_catalogue_limit.cause: A team can have {{0}} template catalogues.
template_catalogue_limit.fix: Remove one it no longer uses, or put the templates of several into one catalogue.

template_not_installable.title: This template cannot be installed
template_not_installable.cause: {{0}} in {{1}} does not pass the checks every template is held to: {{2}}
template_not_installable.fix: Correct the template in the catalogue and refresh it. The catalogue's entry under Templates lists why each template was refused.

git.title: Git
git.help: Connect an account so Skifity can read your private repositories and deploy when you push. A public repository needs none of this.
git.sourceNameHelp: Something you will recognise, such as "Work GitHub".
git.tokenHelp: Needs permission to read the repository and create a webhook, and — to show each deploy on its commit and pull request — to write commit statuses and comments. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
git.baseURLHelp: For a self-hosted GitLab or Gitea. Leave empty for the hosted service.
git.disconnectWarning: Apps deployed from this account stop deploying on push. They keep running.
git.webhookURLHelp: Skifity adds this to your repositories by itself when the token allows it. If it could not, add it by hand in the repository's webhook settings.
git.pushDeploysOn: Pushes to this repository deploy it
git.pushDeploysOnHelp: Skifity added the webhook to your Git host. Nothing else to set up.
git.pushDeploysManual: Deploy on push needs one more step
git.pushDeploysManualHelp: Skifity could not add the webhook itself, so add this URL to the repository's webhook settings, with the secret shown under Settings, Git, Webhook.
git.webhookSecretHelp: Paste this as the webhook's secret. It belongs to this connection alone, so it can be given to a repository without giving away the token.
git.webhookSecretIsToken: This connection was made before each had a secret of its own, so its webhooks are signed with its token. Connect the account again to give it a secret of its own.
git.repositoriesTruncated: Only the {{limit}} most recently active are listed. Type part of a name to narrow them, or paste the address of any other.

bitbucket.workspaceHelp: The part of a repository's address after bitbucket.org/. An access token needs it. With an API token, leave it empty to list every workspace the token can see.
bitbucket.emailHelp: For an API token: the email of the Atlassian account that made it. Leave it empty for an access token, which is sent on its own.
bitbucket.tokenHelp: Make an API token in your Atlassian account settings (Security, then Create API token with scopes, for Bitbucket), or an access token in the repository's or workspace's settings (Access tokens). App passwords no longer work. It needs:
bitbucket.scopeRepositories: Repositories: read (read:repository:bitbucket), to clone, list and mark each deploy on its commit; an API token that lists your workspaces also needs read:workspace:bitbucket.
bitbucket.scopePullRequests: Pull requests: write (read:pullrequest:bitbucket and write:pullrequest:bitbucket), to comment the preview's address on its pull request.
bitbucket.scopeWebhooks: Webhooks: read and write (read:webhook:bitbucket and write:webhook:bitbucket), so Skifity adds the webhook itself.
bitbucket.tokenStored: Skifity asks Bitbucket whether the token works before saving it. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
bitbucket.webhookStepOpen: In the repository, open Repository settings, then Webhooks, then Add webhook.
bitbucket.webhookStepFill: Give it a title, and paste the address above as its URL and the secret above as its Secret.
bitbucket.webhookStepTriggers: Under Triggers, choose from a full list: Repository Push, and Pull Request Created, Updated, Merged and Declined.
bitbucket.webhookStepSave: Save. Bitbucket signs every delivery with the secret, and Skifity refuses any delivery that is not signed.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.help: Where to tell you when something happens. Nothing is sent until you add somewhere.
notifications.eventsHelp: Choose as few as you can live with. A channel nobody reads is worse than none.
notifications.testSent: Sent. If nothing arrives, the details are wrong.

event.certificate.failed: A certificate could not be issued
event.app.alert: An app crossed a usage threshold
event.server.alert: A server crossed a usage threshold
event.backup.missed: A scheduled backup was missed and taken late
event.app.vulnerable: An app's image has a new critical vulnerability
event.app.drifted: An app was changed outside the panel
event.certificate.expiring: One of the team's own certificates is about to expire

notifications.removeConfirm: {{name}} stops receiving notifications, and its address and token are forgotten.

telegram.chat_idHelp: Message your bot once, then read the chat id from getUpdates.

slack.webhook_urlHelp: An incoming webhook, from the Slack app's Incoming Webhooks page. It starts with https://hooks.slack.com/.

mattermost.webhook_urlHelp: An incoming webhook, from Integrations in Mattermost. It ends in /hooks/ and a long id.

ntfy.serverHelp: Leave empty for ntfy.sh, or give your own server's address.
ntfy.tokenHelp: Only for a topic that needs one.

pushover.app_tokenHelp: Create an application at pushover.net to get one.
pushover.user_keyHelp: At the top of your pushover.net dashboard.

webhook.secretHelp: Optional. Sent in the X-Skifity-Secret header, so your receiver can check the request came from here.

teams.webhook_urlHelp: In Teams, open the channel's Workflows and choose "Send webhook alerts to a channel". Paste the link the workflow gives you.

gotify.serverHelp: Your Gotify server's address, such as https://gotify.example.com.
gotify.app_tokenHelp: Create an application under Apps in Gotify, and copy its token.

notifications.noProjectsLeft: Its projects were deleted: only server events reach it
notifications.kindFixed: A channel's kind cannot be changed. Add another channel instead.
notifications.noEventsChosen: None chosen: the channel is sent every event except successful backups.
notifications.limitToProjectsHelp: Events about an app, a database or a backup are sent only from the projects you choose. Events about servers and the panel itself go to every channel, because they affect every project.
notifications.enabledHelp: Switch it off to pause the channel without losing its settings.
notifications.secretStored: Stored. Leave it empty to keep it, or type a new value to replace it.

invite.title: Join {{team}}
invite.subtitle: You have been invited as {{email}}, as a {{role}}. Choose a password and you are in.
invite.emailFixed: This is the address the invitation was for, and it cannot be changed here.
invite.notValidHelp: The link has expired, has been used already, or was withdrawn. Ask whoever invited you for a new one.

environments.confinementRestrictedHelp: Pods here are held to the strictest profile. An image that starts as root is refused, which is most off-the-shelf images.
environments.confinementBaselineHelp: This environment accepts an image that starts as root. A privileged container, host networking and host paths are still refused, so an app still cannot reach the server it runs on.
environments.confinementLowerTitle: Accept images that start as root?
environments.confinementLowerConfirm: Apps in this environment will be allowed to start as root inside their own container, which is what the official WordPress, Nextcloud and MediaWiki images do. A privileged container, host networking, host paths and extra capabilities stay refused. Redeploy each app for the change to reach it.
environments.previewStackHelp: A pull request's preview gets a copy of every app here, not only the ones its repository builds. The others run the version they run here, and apps sharing a database share the preview's copy of it.
environments.cloneHelp: A new environment with the same apps, settings, variables, files, processes and schedules, and a new, empty database of each kind, linked the same way. Data, volume contents, custom domains and public ports stay with the original.
environments.cloneDeploy: Deploy the apps once they are copied
environments.cloneDeployHelp: Otherwise they wait for their first deploy.
environments.cloned: {{name}} is ready. Apps copied: {{apps}}. Databases made: {{databases}}.

cloneNote.volumes_empty: {{name}} has its volumes, empty: their contents stay with the original.
cloneNote.domains_kept: {{name}}'s own domains stay with the original; the copy has the address every new app gets.
cloneNote.ports_kept: {{name}}'s public ports stay with the original: each belongs to one app on the whole panel.
cloneNote.push_deploy_off: {{name}} does not deploy on push until that is turned on in its settings.
cloneNote.database_skipped: The database {{name}} was not copied: this panel has no cluster to make one in.

firewall.title: Firewall
firewall.help: Rules on who may reach this app: by address, by country, by network, by path or by header, combined with and and or. The first rule that matches decides.
firewall.notInstalled: These rules are not being enforced
firewall.notInstalledHelp: The firewall component is not installed, so nothing is checking requests. Install it under Settings, then Components.
firewall.noDomain: This app has no address to guard
firewall.noDomainHelp: Rules apply to a hostname. Add a domain under Domains, and these rules will start applying to it.
firewall.noGeo: A rule names a country or a network, and this panel does not look them up
firewall.noGeoHelp: Turn on "Look up a visitor's country and network" under Settings, then Domains and HTTPS. Until then, a rule like this is skipped on every request.

appPassword.title: Password
appPassword.help: Ask everyone who opens this app for a username and password first. For a staging site, a preview or an internal tool.
appPassword.current: Anyone opening it signs in as {{username}}. Changed {{when}}.
appPassword.removeDescription: Anyone with the address will be able to open this app again.
appPassword.plainHttpHelp: On {{hostnames}} the password crosses the network readable by anyone on the way. Add a domain of your own to give the app a certificate.
appPassword.previews: Previews of this app's pull requests ask for the same password. Only an admin can change it.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.subtitle: Features other people wrote, running beside the panel in a container of their own.
plugins.emptyHelp: Browse the store, or install one from an address or a manifest you paste.
plugins.removeConfirm: Its container, its settings and its access token all go. Anything it wrote elsewhere stays where it is.
plugins.secretStored: Stored. Enter a new value to replace it.
plugins.storeVerified: Signed by the key this panel trusts · {{url}}
plugins.storeUnsigned: Nobody has vouched for this catalogue
plugins.storeUnsignedHelp: No signing key is set, so the panel cannot tell whether this list is the one the store published. Set one under Settings, then Plugins. Either way, what a plugin may do is shown before you install it.
plugins.storeEmpty: The store has nothing in it
plugins.storeEmptyHelp: The catalogue was read and lists no plugins.
plugins.fromAddressHelp: A plugin can always be installed without a store — from the address of its manifest, or by pasting the manifest itself. This is the path a cluster with no way out to the internet uses, and the one a plugin author uses to try their own.
plugins.willBeAbleTo: This plugin will be able to:
plugins.noPermissions: It is not asking for access to anything.
plugins.blocksDeploys: This plugin can stop a deployment
plugins.blocksDeploysHelp: It asked to be consulted before every deploy and may refuse one. A plugin that is down does not block anything, and you can switch it off at any time.
plugins.confinementNote: It runs in a namespace of its own and can reach the panel, DNS and the internet — not your apps, not your databases, and not the server it runs on.
plugins.digestNote: Pinned by digest, so the image cannot be changed under you after you have agreed to it.

needs.databaseCreate: Create a {{engine}} database and connect it as {{variable}}
needs.databaseStarting: A database takes about a minute to start, so the app may restart once while it waits. That is expected.
needs.notProvided: This panel does not run {{engine}}. Use a hosted one and set {{variable}} under Variables.
needs.ephemeralTitle: This app keeps its data in a file
needs.ephemeral: It stores data through {{evidence}} ({{what}}) inside the container, and the next deploy replaces the container. Everything saved there is lost.
needs.ephemeralFixDatabase: Tick the database above and point the app at it instead.
needs.ephemeralFixVolume: Use a managed database instead, or add a volume for its data folder once the app is created.
needs.variablesExpected: This app expects the settings listed in {{source}}. Paste your .env here and they are saved before the first deploy.
needs.variablesOptional: Paste your .env here and its settings are saved before the first deploy.
needs.variablesSecret: Anything that looks like a key or a password is kept secret.
needs.allSet: Every setting this app expects is here.
needs.databaseFailed: The app was created, but its {{engine}} database was not
needs.pastedReplaced: {{variable}} from what you pasted is left out: the {{engine}} database created with the app sets it, pointing at itself rather than at the computer the file came from.

folder.label: Your app's folder
folder.help: Pick the folder your app is in. node_modules, every .env file and whatever .gitignore lists stay on your computer.
folder.dotenvRead: The settings from your folder's .env are in the box below. The file itself is not uploaded: its values are saved as the app's variables, and anything that looks like a key or a password is stored as a secret. Clear the box to leave them out.
folder.emptyTitle: There is nothing to send in that folder
folder.empty: Every file in it is one that stays behind, such as node_modules or a .env. Pick the folder the app's own code is in.
folder.tooLargeTitle: That folder is too large to send

tooLarge.entries: It has more than {{entries}} files, which an app's own code almost never does. The largest parts are:
tooLarge.unpacked: Its files add up to more than {{size}}. The largest parts are:
tooLarge.compressed: Packed, it is more than {{size}}. The largest parts are:

folder.tooLargeFix: A dependency folder, build output or a data file is usually the cause. List it in a .skifityignore file in the folder and pick it again.
folder.sendFailed: The app was created, but its code could not be sent. Send it again from the app's page.
folder.terminalHelp: Run these in the app's folder. The first time, skifity up creates the app, the database it uses and the link to the folder; after that, running it again sends and deploys the new version.
folder.terminalAssistant: An assistant that can run commands can do this for you, or connect to skifity mcp and use its deploy_folder tool.

processes.title: Processes
processes.help: Workers, clocks and anything else that runs beside the app: the same build and variables, a command of their own, and no port, so nothing sends them traffic. Each deploy updates them with the app.
processes.name: Name
processes.removeConfirm: {{name}} stops, and its command is forgotten. Set its instances to 0 instead to stop it and keep the command.
processes.formHelp: The name is lowercase, as in a Procfile: worker, clock. The same name again changes its command and keeps its instances. 0 instances stops a process and keeps it.
processes.detectedHelp: Ticked ones run beside the app from its first deploy, on the same build. Untick one to leave it out; it can be added later under Scaling.

k3s.title: Kubernetes (k3s)
k3s.help: The version every server runs. An upgrade goes one minor version at a time, the control plane before the workers, one server at a time.
k3s.upToDate: Every server already runs this version.
k3s.releasesUnavailable: The list of k3s releases could not be read. Type the version instead, as it is written on the k3s releases page.
k3s.confirm: Each server is cordoned, upgraded and brought back in turn, the control plane first. It cannot be undone from here: k3s is not downgraded.
k3s.started: The upgrade has started. Each server's version changes here and on the Servers page as it is done.

reason.not_a_release: {{target}} is not a k3s release; they are written like v1.31.4+k3s1.
reason.unknown_version: {{server}} reports {{version}}, which is not a k3s version this can reason about.
reason.downgrade: {{server}} already runs {{version}}, newer than {{target}}; k3s is not downgraded.
reason.major: {{server}} runs {{version}}, a different major version from {{target}}.
reason.not_ready: {{server}} is not ready. Every server has to be, since each is taken out in turn and has to come back.
reason.skips_minor: {{target}} skips {{next}}. Kubernetes is upgraded one minor version at a time, so upgrade to the latest {{next}} first.
reason.no_backup: There is no backup of the panel's own database from the last day. Take one first, under Backups of this panel: it is what the panel is restored from if an upgrade takes its server with it.
reason.one_control_plane: There is one control plane, so the Kubernetes API is unreachable for about a minute while it restarts. Apps keep serving, and the panel reconnects by itself.
reason.only_server: This is the only server. Nothing new is scheduled while it is cordoned, so a deploy during the upgrade waits for it.
reason.other_plans: Upgrade plans the panel did not write are already in the cluster ({{plans}}); two sets would upgrade servers side by side. Remove them first: kubectl -n system-upgrade delete plans.upgrade.cattle.io {{plans}}
reason.plans_unreadable: The upgrade plans already in the cluster could not be read: {{error}}

note.dockerfile: Found {{file}}, so it is used as-is.
note.compose_empty: No services were found in it.
note.compose_pick: Skifity runs one service per app, so pick the service this app is. Create the others the same way, in the same environment, where they reach each other by name.
note.unknown: Skifity could not tell what this repository is written in.
note.unknown_try: It will try the zero-config builder, which may still work. If it does not, add a Dockerfile.
note.package_json_unparsable: package.json could not be parsed, so the defaults are used.
note.next_port: Next.js listens on port 3000 by default.
note.vite_static: This looks like a front-end build: `npm run build` runs and the files it writes to `dist` are served directly, with no Node process in the image.
note.cra_static: Create React App writes to `build`, which is served directly.
note.angular_static: Angular writes to `dist/<project>`; check the directory under Source if the site comes up empty.
note.start_script: The `start` script from package.json is used to run the app.
note.no_start_script: package.json has no `start` script, so the builder has to guess how to run this. Adding one makes the deploy predictable.
note.node_version: Node version {{version}} is requested by package.json.
note.django: Django needs DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and ALLOWED_HOSTS set, and collectstatic run during the build.
note.flask: Flask's built-in server is not meant for production; the builder runs it behind gunicorn.
note.go_binary: Go builds to a single binary, so the image will be small.
note.go_port: Read the port from the PORT environment variable rather than hardcoding one.
note.laravel: Laravel needs APP_KEY set. Generate one with `php artisan key:generate --show` and add it as a secret.
note.wordpress: WordPress writes uploads to disk, so add a volume for wp-content/uploads before scaling past one instance.
note.php_no_composer: There is no composer.json, so this was detected from the .php files alone.
note.rails: Rails needs SECRET_KEY_BASE set, and RAILS_SERVE_STATIC_FILES=true unless something else serves the assets.
note.rust: Rust builds take a while the first time; later builds reuse the cache.
note.spring: The JVM needs a memory limit it knows about; the builder sets -XX:MaxRAMPercentage so it respects the container's limit.
note.static: The files are served by a small web server; no application process runs.
note.procfile_release: The Procfile's release line runs after each build and before the new version takes traffic.
note.procfile_bad_name: The Procfile's {{name}} line cannot be a process under that name: add it on the app's page under a lowercase name of up to 20 letters, digits and hyphens.
note.procfile_processes: The Procfile also names {{names}}, which run beside the app as its processes: the same build and variables, a command of their own, no port.
note.app_json_postdeploy: app.json's postdeploy script, `{{command}}`, becomes the seed for previews: it runs once in each new one. Run it here once with `skifity run -- {{command}}`.
note.procfile_same_name: The Procfile's {{name}} line is left out: it becomes {{as}} here, which an earlier line already is.
note.procfile_over_limit: An app runs at most {{max}} processes beside web, so the Procfile's {{names}} lines are left out. A Procfile with that many is usually several apps sharing a repository.

cert-manager.title: HTTPS certificates
cert-manager.description: Issues and renews Let's Encrypt certificates for your domains.

registry.title: Image registry
registry.description: Stores the images Skifity builds, inside the cluster.

buildkit.title: Builder
buildkit.description: Builds your apps into images, without needing Docker on the host.

cloudnative-pg.title: PostgreSQL
cloudnative-pg.description: Runs and looks after PostgreSQL databases, including backups and failover.

keda.title: Scale to zero
keda.description: Stops idle apps and starts them again on the first request. The HTTP add-on is beta upstream.

longhorn.title: Cross-node storage
longhorn.description: Replicates volumes between servers so an app with storage survives a node failure. Uses a noticeable amount of memory on every node.

firewall.title: Firewall
firewall.description: Rules on who may reach an app: by address, by country, by network, by path or by header, combined with and and or. Needs Traefik, which k3s installs by default.

cloudflare-tunnel.title: Cloudflare tunnel
cloudflare-tunnel.description: Puts your apps on the internet with no public IP and no port open, through Cloudflare. Needs a tunnel token in Settings, under Domains and HTTPS.

system-upgrade.title: Kubernetes upgrades
system-upgrade.description: Upgrades k3s on every server, one at a time, when you ask for it under Settings. Installed with the first upgrade.

monitoring.title: Full monitoring
monitoring.description: Prometheus and Grafana, installed with Helm rather than by the panel. Skifity shows CPU and memory for every server and every instance without it.

files.title: Files
files.help: Configuration the app reads from a file — an nginx.conf, a Caddyfile, a script run at start. Each is mounted read-only at its path in every container the app runs.
files.empty: No files. The app runs with what its image holds.
files.removeConfirm: {{path}} is removed from the app's containers, and the app restarts without it.
files.pathHelp: Where the file appears in the container, from /. The rest of that directory is still the image's.
files.secretHelp: Never shown again once saved, and not given to a preview of a pull request from a fork.
files.secretStored: Saved and hidden. Type new content to replace it.
files.executableHelp: For a script the image runs, such as one in /docker-entrypoint.d.
files.restartNote: Saving restarts the app so it reads the file. It does not rebuild it.

registries.title: Private registries
registries.help: Credentials for the registries your private images live in. Every app in the team pulls with them, and every build pulls its base image with them.
registries.empty: None. Public images need nothing here.
registries.formHelp: ghcr.io, docker.io or your own registry's host. Use a token that can only read packages rather than an account's password. The registry is asked before anything is saved.
registries.unchecked: Saved, but {{host}} could not be asked from the panel.
registries.removeConfirm: Apps stop pulling from {{host}} with these credentials from their next deploy.

ports.title: Ports that are not HTTP
ports.help: For a game server, an MQTT broker or anything else that is not a website: the port is opened on every server. The firewall does not apply to these.
ports.empty: None. The app is reached through its domains.
ports.publicPortHelp: The same as the app's port when left empty. Each public port is open for one app on the whole panel.
ports.closeConfirm: {{port}} closes on every server, and whatever connects to it is refused.

previews.previewBranchHelp: A copy of this app, built from the branch, in a preview environment of its own with its own databases — the same preview a pull request from that branch gets, so opening one later updates this instead of making another.
previews.previewBranchRemove: It stays until the branch is deleted, its pull request is closed, or somebody closes it with skifity preview --close.

security.title: Known vulnerabilities
security.help: The image this app runs, checked with Trivy against published advisories: when it is built or deployed, again every day, and whenever you ask.
security.queued: Waiting for the scanner, which looks at one image at a time.
security.running: Scanning the image. This usually takes a minute or two.
security.disabled: Image scanning is switched off for this panel. An administrator can turn it on under Settings, Image scanning.
security.never: This app's image has not been scanned yet.
security.notDeployed: The app has not been deployed yet. Its image is scanned once it is built.
security.failed: The last scan did not finish
security.notCurrent: This report is of another image than the one the app runs now. Scan now to check the one it runs.
security.undeployed: This report is of an image that has not gone out: its deploy is under way, or was stopped.
security.clean: No known vulnerabilities were found in this image.
security.noneFixable: None of these has a fix yet.
security.more: {{number}} more, less severe, were not kept in the report.
security.blocked: Deploys of this image are stopped
security.blockedHelp: This panel stops a deploy whose image has a critical vulnerability with a fix, and this image has {{number}}. Move to the fixed versions and deploy again, or use Deploy anyway on the stopped deployment; that is recorded in the activity log.

drift.noticeBody: Some of this app's settings in the cluster were changed outside the panel, with kubectl or another tool. Advanced shows what changed, and puts it back.
drift.title: Changed outside {{product}}
drift.help: Every few minutes the panel compares this app's objects in the cluster with what it applies, on the fields it sets. A change made with kubectl or another tool is listed here, with who made it.
drift.notDeployed: Nothing is deployed yet, so there is nothing to compare.
drift.hidden: A secret value differs. Neither value is shown.
drift.repairConfirm: The app's objects are applied again as {{product}} applies them, which undoes the changes listed. Nothing is built and no deployment is recorded. If the running version was changed, its instances are replaced one at a time.
drift.repaired: Put back as the panel applies it.
drift.autoRepairHelp: When the panel finds a change, it puts the app back by itself and says so. Off by default: a change somebody made on purpose, during an incident, is not something to undo behind their back.
drift.applying: {{product}} is changing this app right now. It is compared again once the deploy or the change has finished.

events.title: What Kubernetes said
events.help: Events the scheduler, the servers and the controllers wrote about this app's objects, newest first. Kubernetes keeps them for about an hour.
events.databaseHelp: Events the scheduler, the servers and the controllers wrote about this database's objects, newest first. Kubernetes keeps them for about an hour.
events.emptyWarnings: No warnings in the last hour
events.emptyHelp: Kubernetes keeps events for about an hour. The list refreshes itself while it is open.

explain.scheduling_cpu_memory: No server has enough free CPU and memory for this instance. Lower what it reserves under Scaling, or add a server.
explain.scheduling_cpu: No server has enough free CPU for this instance. Lower the CPU it reserves under Scaling, or add a server.
explain.scheduling_memory: No server has enough free memory for this instance. Lower the memory it reserves under Scaling, or add a server.
explain.scheduling_volume: This app's volume has not been created yet. On a single server that is usually a storage class that is still starting; across servers it means no server can provide the volume.
explain.scheduling_taint: The only servers with room are not accepting apps. A control-plane server does not run apps unless you allow it, and a server being drained accepts nothing.
explain.scheduling_node_affinity: No server matches where this app is allowed to run.
explain.scheduling_anti_affinity: Every server already runs an instance of this app. Add a server, or run fewer instances.
explain.scheduling_unexplained: No server can take this instance: {{0}}
explain.scheduling_waiting: Waiting for a server with room for this instance.
explain.replicas_quota: This environment has reached its limit, so no more instances can start. Raise the environment's limits, or give this app less. ({{0}})
explain.replicas_pod_security: The instance was refused by the cluster's security rules: {{0}}
explain.replicas_failed: The instances could not be created.
explain.pull_unauthorized: The registry refused to hand over the image. If it is a private registry, set its credentials under Settings, then Registry.
explain.pull_missing: That image is not in the registry. If this is a rollback to an old version, its image has been removed to keep the disk free; deploy the commit again instead.
explain.pull_unreachable: The registry could not be reached from the server. Check the address, and that the server has a route to it.
explain.pull_failed: The image could not be pulled: {{0}}
explain.pull_failed_empty: The image could not be pulled.
explain.runs_as_root: This image starts as root and drops privileges itself, which is ordinary for an off-the-shelf container and is what this environment refuses. Change the environment's confinement to "baseline" under the project, then deploy again. Baseline still refuses a privileged container, host networking and host paths, so the app still cannot reach the server it runs on.
explain.named_user: This image names its user ({{0}}) instead of numbering it, so the cluster cannot check that it is not root, and this environment refuses what it cannot check. Set "Run as user" in the app's settings to that user's number — 65534 for nobody — and deploy again, or change the environment's confinement to "baseline" under the project.
explain.crash_backoff: The app keeps stopping soon after it starts, so Kubernetes waits longer before each restart. Why it stopped is in its log from before the restart: open Logs, then Before the restart.
explain.probe_readiness: The health check failed, so this instance is sent no traffic until it passes. Check the health check's path and port under Settings, and that the app answers there in time.
explain.probe_liveness: The health check kept failing, so the instance is being restarted. A check that is slow or points at the wrong path restarts an app that is working: check it under Settings.
explain.probe_startup: The app did not pass its health check in the time it is given to start. If it starts slowly, give it longer under Settings; otherwise its logs say why it is not answering.
explain.mount_config_missing: The instance cannot start because configuration it reads is missing from the cluster: {{0}}. Put the app back under Advanced, or deploy again, and it is written again.
explain.mount_failed: A volume could not be mounted. A volume is used by one server at a time: if an instance on another server still holds it, this one waits until that instance stops.
explain.attach_failed: The storage behind a volume could not be attached to this server. It is usually still attached to another server, and is released once that server lets it go.
explain.sandbox_failed: The server could not set up this instance's network or container. That is a problem on the server rather than in the app: if it goes on, restart k3s on that server, or remove the server and add it again.
explain.oom: The app used more memory than its limit and was stopped. Raise the memory limit under Scaling, or find what is using the memory.
explain.evicted: The server ran short and stopped this instance to protect itself: {{0}} It is started again on a server with room.

certificates.title: Your own certificates
certificates.help: Certificates you bring instead of Let's Encrypt's: a company CA's, an EV or OV certificate, a wildcard bought elsewhere, or one for a hostname Let's Encrypt cannot reach. Every HTTPS domain in the team that one covers is served with it.
certificates.empty: None. Every HTTPS domain gets its certificate from Let's Encrypt.
certificates.name: Name
certificates.nameHelp: Uploading under a name that exists replaces that certificate, which is how a renewal goes in.
certificates.chainHelp: Your certificate and the intermediate certificates that came with it, PEM, in any order.
certificates.keyHelp: PEM, without a passphrase. It is encrypted as it arrives and never shown again, here or anywhere.
certificates.reordered: The certificates were put in order, yours first.
certificates.updating_one: {{count}} app is being updated to use it.
certificates.updating_other: {{count}} apps are being updated to use it.
certificates.removeConfirm_one: It serves {{count}} domain, which goes back to Let's Encrypt.
certificates.removeConfirm_other: It serves {{count}} domains, which go back to Let's Encrypt.
certificates.removeConsequence: A hostname Let's Encrypt cannot reach stops working over HTTPS, and the panel keeps no other copy of the private key.
certificates.noDomains: No domain in the team uses it yet.
